column3: Restaurant. 餐 is "meal" and 馆 a public building, the kind of place that serves or houses something; the same 馆 ends 宾馆 "hotel" and 博物馆 "museum". Typical use: 开餐馆 "run a restaurant", 去餐馆吃饭 "eat out". It is the neutral word for any sit-down eatery, from a small shop to a big place.
column6: Zhè jiā cānguǎn de cài hěn hǎochī.
column7: The food at this restaurant is very good.

column3: Food and beverage, the catering trade as a business: 餐饮业 "the catering industry", 餐饮服务 "food service". It is a written, business word; to talk about eating out in daily speech people say 吃饭 or 餐馆. 餐 is "meal" and 饮 "drink", so the word covers both food and drinks.
column4: 他在餐饮行业工作了十年。
column5: 他在餐飲行業工作了十年。
column6: Tā zài cānyǐn hángyè gōngzuò le shí nián.
column7: He has worked in the catering industry for ten years.

column3: Diet, what and how one eats and drinks, used when talking about health or customs: 饮食习惯 "eating habits", 饮食健康 "a healthy diet", 注意饮食 "watch what you eat". 饮 is "drink" and 食 "food"; 食 is a lidded dish of food, and it turns into the 饣 on the left of 饭, 馆 and 饼. A more formal word than 吃.
column4: 健康的饮食对身体很重要。
column5: 健康的飲食對身體很重要。
column6: Jiànkāng de yǐnshí duì shēntǐ hěn zhòngyào.
column7: A healthy diet is very important for the body.

column3: On the mainland, "baijiu", the strong clear spirit distilled from grain, usually sorghum, drunk in small cups at banquets. It is 白 "white/clear" plus 酒 "alcohol". White wine is a different word, 白葡萄酒.
column6: Tā hē le yīdiǎn báijiǔ.
column7: He drank a little baijiu.

column3: Wine made from grapes, 葡萄 "grape" + 酒 "alcohol". Measure word 瓶 for a bottle, 杯 for a glass: 一杯葡萄酒. Wine is also called 红酒 (red wine) in everyday speech; 白葡萄酒 is "white wine" and 红葡萄酒 "red wine". Both 葡 and 萄 have the grass top 艹 and are only used in this one word.
column6: Zhè píng pútáojiǔ shì Fǎguó de.
column7: This bottle of wine is from France.

column3: Drunkard, a rude, spoken word. 鬼 "ghost" is also a suffix for people with a habit they cannot give up: 酒鬼, 烟鬼 "chain smoker", 懒鬼 "lazybones". The ghost in the character has a scary face on top of a kneeling body. Do not use it of a person to their face.
column6: Tā bàba shì ge jiǔguǐ.
column7: His father is a drunkard.

column3: Drunk. Almost always as the result of drinking: 喝醉 "drink until drunk", 醉了 "be drunk", 喝得大醉. The left part 酉 is a wine jar and appears in many drink words (酒, 酸, 醉); the right part 卒 is the sound. It can also be figurative, "intoxicated" by something beautiful: 陶醉.
column6: Tā hēzuì le, hái zài chànggē.
column7: He is drunk and still singing.

column3: A "flat, round cake" of any kind: a pancake, a flatbread or a pastry. 煎饼 and 烙饼 are common northern breakfast foods, and 饼 is the base of words like 饼干 and 月饼. Measure word 张 for a flat one, 块 for a piece. The food radical 饣 on the left shows the category.
column6: Zǎoshang wǒ chī le yī zhāng bǐng.
column7: This morning I ate a flatbread.

column3: Biscuit, cookie, cracker: 饼 "cake" + 干 "dry". Here 干 is read gān, the "dry" 干 (traditional 乾), not the gàn of 干活. Measure word 块 or 片 for one, 包 for a packet: 一包饼干. It covers both sweet and salty ones.
column6: Háizi xǐhuan chī bǐnggān.
column7: Children like to eat cookies.

column3: Mooncake, the round pastry eaten at the Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节), often filled with lotus seed paste or egg yolk. It is 月 "moon" + 饼 "cake", named for the round shape. Typical use: 吃月饼, 送月饼 "give mooncakes as gifts", 一盒月饼.
column4: 中秋节我们一起吃月饼。
column5: 中秋節我們一起吃月餅。
column6: Zhōngqiūjié wǒmen yīqǐ chī yuèbǐng.
column7: At the Mid-Autumn Festival we eat mooncakes together.

column3: Sushi, borrowed from Japanese: the two characters are the way Japanese writes the word, read here with their Chinese sounds. They carry no meaning of "sushi" on their own: 寿 is "long life" as in 长寿, and 司 "to manage". Typical use: 吃寿司, 寿司店, 一份寿司.
column6: Wǒmen zhōngwǔ qù chī shòusī ba.
column7: Let's go and eat sushi at noon.

column3: Roast duck, above all Beijing roast duck (北京烤鸭), served with thin pancakes, spring onion and sauce. 烤 is "to roast or bake" (火 fire + 考, which still sounds like kǎo) and 鸭 is "duck". 烤 also builds 烤肉, 烤鸡, 烤面包 "toast".
column6: Lái Běijīng yīdìng yào chī kǎoyā.
column7: When you come to Beijing you must eat roast duck.

column3: Barbecued or roast meat, and also the verb "to barbecue": 去野外烤肉 "go barbecue outdoors". In Korean restaurants 韩国烤肉 is Korean barbecue. In Taiwan 烤肉 is also the family barbecue held at the Mid-Autumn Festival. 烤 "roast" + 肉 "meat".
column4: 周末我们去吃韩国烤肉。
column5: 週末我們去吃韓國烤肉。
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù chī Hánguó kǎoròu.
column7: At the weekend we are going to eat Korean barbecue.

column3: A boxed meal, rice with dishes in a partitioned box, sold at stations, on trains, or delivered to offices at lunchtime. Counted with 份: 一份盒饭. It is 盒 "box" + 饭 "cooked rice, meal". The sound part of 盒 is 合, which has the same he sound in its first tone.
column4: 中午我们订了三份盒饭。
column5: 中午我們訂了三份盒飯。
column6: Zhōngwǔ wǒmen dìng le sān fèn héfàn.
column7: At noon we ordered three boxed meals.

column3: To taste, to try a food, and by extension to experience something. Doubled it means "have a taste": 尝尝 (the second one neutral), 尝一尝. The result form is 尝到 "to taste/experience": 尝到了甜头. It also appears in 尝试 "to attempt". The traditional form for the tasting sense is 嚐 in Taiwan.
column6: Nǐ chángchang zhège cài.
column7: Try this dish.

column3: Literally "sour, sweet, bitter, hot", the four flavors, and figuratively "all the joys and sorrows of life": 尝遍了人生的酸甜苦辣. As a set phrase it has no particles and is more often figurative than about food. 辣 means "hot, spicy" with 辛 on the left, the same part as in 辛苦.
column6: Shēnghuó lǐ yǒu suāntiánkǔlà.
column7: Life has its sours, sweets, bitters and spices.

column3: A fork: 用叉子吃面 "eat noodles with a fork". 叉 is the base word and 子 a noun suffix in the neutral tone. The set of cutlery is 刀叉 "knife and fork"; chopsticks are 筷子. In the character, a hand 又 grasps something small, the dot.
column4: 我不会用筷子，我用叉子。
column5: 我不會用筷子，我用叉子。
column6: Wǒ bù huì yòng kuàizi, wǒ yòng chāzi.
column7: I can't use chopsticks, so I use a fork.

column3: Used alone, "fork" in the sense of a prong or pitchfork, and "a cross, an X". As a verb it means "to cross" or "to jam in": 叉腰 "put hands on hips", 交叉 "intersect". The mark X for a wrong answer is 叉, written as 打叉 or 画叉. Eating forks are normally 叉子.
column4: 老师在错题上画了一个叉。
column5: 老師在錯題上畫了一個叉。
column6: Lǎoshī zài cuòtí shàng huà le yī gè chā.
column7: The teacher drew a cross next to the wrong questions.

column3: Vegetables, the general and slightly more formal word: 新鲜蔬菜, 多吃蔬菜. In everyday speech 菜 alone or 青菜 is common. Both characters have the grass top 艹: 蔬 with 疏 for sound, 菜 with 采. Measure words are used for specific vegetables, not for 蔬菜 itself.
column6: Duō chī shūcài duì shēntǐ hǎo.
column7: Eating more vegetables is good for you.

column3: Potato, literally "earth bean": 土 "earth, soil" + 豆 "bean". Typical dishes are 炒土豆丝 and 土豆炖牛肉. Watch the dialect difference: in Taiwan 土豆 means "peanut"; there a potato is 马铃薯. 豆 is a picture of a tall serving dish.
column4: 他今天晚上做了土豆牛肉。
column5: 他今天晚上做了土豆牛肉。
column6: Tā jīntiān wǎnshang zuò le tǔdòu niúròu.
column7: This evening he made beef with potatoes.

column3: Tomato, literally "western red persimmon". A staple of home cooking, with eggs in 西红柿炒鸡蛋 and in soups. In Taiwan the usual word is 番茄. The last character 柿 has 木 "tree" on the left and 市 on the right, which gives the sound shì.
column4: 西红柿炒鸡蛋是一道家常菜。
column5: 西紅柿炒雞蛋是一道家常菜。
column6: Xīhóngshì chǎo jīdàn shì yī dào jiācháng cài.
column7: Tomato with scrambled egg is a home-style dish.

column3: Grape: 一串葡萄 "a bunch of grapes", 葡萄干 "raisin", 葡萄酒 "wine". A two-character word whose halves mean nothing alone; both have the grass top 艹. The second syllable is neutral tone in speech, pútao. The word is borrowed from a foreign language.
column6: Zhèxiē pútao yòu dà yòu tián.
column7: These grapes are big and sweet.

column3: Peach. The right part 兆 is the sound and still rhymes: táo and zhào. Peaches stand for long life; at a birthday of an older person people give 寿桃 "longevity peaches" (buns shaped like peaches). 桃 is the base of 桃花 "peach blossom" and 桃树 "peach tree"; the fruit is also called 桃子.
column4: 这棵树上的桃已经熟了。
column5: 這棵樹上的桃已經熟了。
column6: Zhè kē shù shàng de táo yǐjīng shú le.
column7: The peaches on this tree are already ripe.

column3: Pear. 利 on top is the sound part and 木 "tree" the meaning part. A pear cannot be shared between two people, as 分梨 sounds like 分离 "to part", a folk belief among couples. Measure word 个; the fruit is also 梨子 in spoken Chinese: 削梨 "peel a pear".
column6: Zhège lí yòu cuì yòu tián.
column7: This pear is crisp and sweet.

column3: Soy or bean products: tofu, soy milk, dried bean curd. The word is built on 制品 "manufactured product", with 豆 "bean". The traditional spelling is 豆製品, because the simplified 制 stands for both 製 "to make" and 制 "system". The pattern X + 品 names a type of product: 豆制品, 水产品, 农产品.
column4: 豆制品里有很多蛋白质。
column5: 豆製品裡有很多蛋白質。
column6: Dòuzhìpǐn lǐ yǒu hěn duō dànbáizhì.
column7: Bean products contain a lot of protein.

column3: Aquatic products: fish, shrimp, crabs, shellfish and seaweed, as sold or traded. A trade and market word: 水产品市场 "seafood market", 水产品加工. 水产 means "products of the water", plus 品 "goods", which is three 口 stacked to suggest many items.
column4: 这个市场有各种水产品。
column5: 這個市場有各種水產品。
column6: Zhège shìchǎng yǒu gèzhǒng shuǐchǎnpǐn.
column7: This market has all kinds of aquatic products.

column3: Agricultural products: grain, vegetables, fruit, meat sold as farm output. It goes with trade and policy language: 农产品价格 "farm product prices", 农产品出口, 绿色农产品. 产 in the traditional form 產 has 生 "to be born" inside, "what is produced";
column4: 农产品的价格最近上涨了。
column5: 農產品的價格最近上漲了。
column6: Nóngchǎnpǐn de jiàgé zuìjìn shàngzhǎng le.
column7: The price of farm produce has risen recently.

column3: Sausage: 香 "fragrant" + 肠 "intestine, casing". Grilled sausages are a snack on the street and at night markets, and 腊肠 is Chinese cured sausage. 肠 has the flesh radical ⺼ on the left, as in other body-part characters (腿, 脑). Counted with 根: 一根香肠.
column6: Zǎofàn tā chī le liǎng gēn xiāngcháng.
column7: For breakfast he ate two sausages.

column3: Ham, literally "fire leg": 火 "fire" + 腿 "leg". Cured ham such as 金华火腿 is a famous Chinese food, and the word also covers the sliced ham in a sandwich: 火腿三明治. The flesh radical ⺼ on 腿 appears in other body words, and 退 on the right gives the sound (tuì, tuǐ).
column6: Wǒ yào yī gè huǒtuǐ sānmíngzhì.
column7: I'd like a ham sandwich.

column3: A bumper harvest: 丰 "abundant" + 收 "to gather in". It is used for crops and, figuratively, for big gains: 大丰收, 喜获丰收, 丰收年. Usually as a verb in a clause: 今年丰收了. The simplified 丰 is a simple picture of an ear of grass.
column6: Jīnnián de píngguǒ fēngshōu le.
column7: There was a bumper apple harvest this year.

column3: Crisp, crunchy for food: 又香又脆 "fragrant and crisp". It also describes a clear, sharp sound: 清脆 "clear and ringing", as in a bell or voice, and "brittle, fragile": 脆弱 "fragile, weak". In speech 干脆 means "simply, just", with 脆 as "clean, neat".
column4: 炸鸡外面很脆，里面很嫩。
column5: 炸雞外面很脆，裡面很嫩。
column6: Zhàjī wàimiàn hěn cuì, lǐmiàn hěn nèn.
column7: The fried chicken is crispy outside and tender inside.

column3: As a verb "to freeze" and "to feel very cold": 冻死了 "freezing to death", 冻手 "hands that are numb with cold", 冰冻 "frozen". In a result clause: 冻得发抖 "shiver with cold". It is also "jelly, aspic" as in 果冻 "fruit jelly". The ice radical 冫 on the left is a sign of cold.
column4: 外面太冷了，我冻得发抖。
column5: 外面太冷了，我凍得發抖。
column6: Wàimiàn tài lěng le, wǒ dòng de fādǒu.
column7: It is so cold outside that I am shivering.

column3: House, room, mostly in compounds (屋子, 房屋, 屋顶 "roof") and a few set phrases. On its own it is a written or somewhat regional word: 一间屋 "a room", 进屋 "come into the room". In the character, the 尸 on top is an old roof shape and 至 below is "to arrive", so the whole is "to stop under a roof".
column6: Zhè jiān wū tài xiǎo le.
column7: This room is too small.

column3: Bedroom. 卧 is "to lie down" (a person 卜 next to 臣, which is an eye here) and 室 is "room", a roof 宀 over 至, the same 室 as in 教室 "classroom" and 办公室 "office". Typical pattern: 在卧室睡觉. A bedroom in a flat is also called 房间 or 卧房.
column6: Wǒ de wòshì zài èr lóu.
column7: My bedroom is on the second floor.

column3: Living room, literally the "guest hall": 客 "guest" (a roof 宀 over 各) + 厅 "hall". It is the room where guests are received and the family sits and watches TV: 在客厅看电视. Flats are described by their rooms, such as 两室一厅 "two bedrooms and a living room".
column6: Háizimen zài kètīng kàn diànshì.
column7: The children are watching TV in the living room.

column3: Kitchen. 厨 means "cook, kitchen" (in traditional characters 廚) and 房 "room" has 户 "door" with 方 as a sound part. 房 also builds 房间 "room", 房子 "house" and 书房 "study". Typical: 在厨房做饭 "cook in the kitchen".
column6: Māma zhèngzài chúfáng zuòfàn.
column7: Mom is cooking in the kitchen.

column3: A hall or lobby: the big open room at the entrance of a hotel, station, airport or office building. 在大厅等 is a common way to say "wait at the lobby". It is different from 客厅, which is the living room of a home. 大 "big" + 厅 "hall".
column6: Wǒmen zài jiǔdiàn dàtīng děng nǐ.
column7: We'll wait for you in the hotel lobby.

column3: A hall, used in compounds for a large public room or a room of the home: 客厅 "living room", 餐厅 "dining hall, restaurant", 大厅 "lobby". By itself it is also a government office level under a province: 教育厅 "Department of Education".
column6: Wǒmen zài zhè jiā cāntīng chīfàn.
column7: We are eating at this restaurant.

column3: A wall, the surface of a room's wall rather than a fence: 墙壁上挂着画 "pictures hang on the wall". 墙 (a plain wall, 一堵墙) and 壁 both have 土 "earth" as meaning, since walls were once built of earth. The word is somewhat written; 墙 alone is more common in speech.
column6: Qiángbì shàng guà zhe yī fú huà.
column7: A painting hangs on the wall.

column3: Next door, the neighbor: 隔壁邻居, 住在隔壁, 隔壁的房间. It works as a noun for the next-door home and as a modifier. 隔 "to separate" has the wall radical 阝 on the left, and 壁 is "wall": "separated by a wall".
column6: Gébì zhù zhe yī wèi lǎorén.
column7: An old person lives next door.

column3: Window curtains. Typical verbs: 拉窗帘 "draw the curtains", 拉开 "open them", 挂窗帘 "hang them". 窗 has a hole 穴 on top, and 帘 has the same 穴 over the cloth 巾. Curtains are also sold as a set: 一套窗帘.
column6: Qǐng bǎ chuānglián lākāi.
column7: Please open the curtains.

column3: Cupboard, cabinet: any piece of furniture with doors or drawers for storing things, like 衣柜 "wardrobe" and 鞋柜 "shoe cabinet". 子 is a neutral-tone suffix. The wood radical 木 shows the material. The same 柜 forms 柜台 "counter".
column6: Yīfu zài guìzi lǐ.
column7: The clothes are in the cupboard.

column3: Bookcase: 书 "book" + 柜 "cabinet". Typical: 书柜里有很多书 "the bookcase has many books", 一个书柜. In 书, the simplified form is a hand holding a brush; the traditional 書 shows it more clearly.
column6: Shūguì lǐ yǒu hěn duō Zhōngwén shū.
column7: There are many Chinese books in the bookcase.

column3: A desk for reading and writing: 书 "book" + 桌 "table". On its own 桌子 is a table. 桌 has 木 "wood" below and 卓 above, which gives the sound zhuō. Typical: 坐在书桌前, 书桌上, 整理书桌.
column6: Tā de shūzhuō zǒngshì hěn luàn.
column7: His desk is always messy.

column3: Glass, the material: 玻璃窗 "glass window", 玻璃杯 "glass cup". Both characters have 王 on the left, which is the jade radical 玉 in a short form, as glass was once treated as a kind of precious stone. The second syllable is neutral in speech: bōli. A counted piece is 块玻璃.
column6: Chuānghu de bōli suì le.
column7: The glass of the window is broken.

column3: A washbowl or basin for washing the face and hands: 脸 "face" + 盆 "basin". 盆 is a dish 皿 with 分 for the sound. A 脸盆 is often a plastic or enamel basin at home or in a dormitory. Counted with 个: 一个脸盆. The common verb for washing the face is 洗脸.
column6: Tā bǎ shuǐ dàojìn liǎnpén lǐ.
column7: She poured the water into the basin.

column3: A pool, pond or basin, something dug out or built to hold water: 小池子, 池子里有鱼. The 池 on its own turns up in words such as 游泳池 "swimming pool", 水池 "tank" and 电池 "battery". 氵 "water" is the meaning part and 也 the sound. 池子 can also mean "dance floor".
column6: Yuànzi lǐ yǒu yī gè xiǎo chízi.
column7: There is a small pond in the yard.

column3: A pot, pan or wok: 炒锅 "frying pan/wok", 火锅 "hotpot", 一口锅 (measure word 口 for woks). Figuratively 背锅 "take the blame". The metal radical 钅 shows what it is made of; the sound part 呙 is much altered from the traditional 鍋 and no longer helps with guō.
column6: Guō lǐ de tāng kuài kāi le.
column7: The soup in the pot is about to boil.

column3: Electric rice cooker: 电 "electric" + 饭 "rice, meal" + 锅 "pot". A basic kitchen item: 用电饭锅煮饭 "cook rice in a rice cooker". The traditional 電 has 雨 "rain" over 申 "lightning".
column6: Wǒ yòng diànfànguō zhǔfàn.
column7: I cook rice in a rice cooker.

column3: A small box or case, and as a measure word for boxed things: 一盒巧克力 "a box of chocolates", 一盒牛奶 "a carton of milk". Alone it is mostly a measure word; the thing is 盒子. 皿 "dish" at the bottom shows a container and 合 on top gives the sound hé.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī hé qiǎokèlì.
column7: I bought a box of chocolates.

column3: A box or case, usually small, which can be closed: 铅笔盒 "pencil case", 礼品盒 "gift box". It is the everyday noun, as 盒 alone is a measure word. The neutral 子 follows. In the north 盒子 can also be a kind of savory filled pie, but that is rare.
column6: Hézi lǐ shì shénme?
column7: What is in the box?

column3: A basin, bowl or pot, and a measure word for what sits in one: 一盆花 "a pot of flowers", 一盆水 "a basin of water". Related words are 花盆 "flower pot", 脸盆 "washbowl" and 盆地 "basin (land)". The dish radical 皿 is at the bottom and 分 on top gives the sound.
column6: Yángtái shàng yǒu yī pén huā.
column7: There is a pot of flowers on the balcony.

column3: A match for lighting a fire: 划火柴 "strike a match", 一根火柴, 一盒火柴. 火 is "fire" and 柴 is "firewood", so the word is "fire sticks". 柴 has 木 "wood" below and 此 on top as a sound part. Lighters are 打火机.
column6: Wǒ zhǎo bu dào huǒchái le.
column7: I can't find the matches.

column3: Coal: 烧煤 "burn coal", 一吨煤, 煤矿 "coal mine". The fire radical 火 and the sound part 某 (mǒu) show the character, and the two sounds méi and mǒu are close. Words with 煤 are often tied to heating and energy, such as 煤炭 and 煤气.
column4: 这个城市冬天用煤取暖。
column5: 這個城市冬天用煤取暖。
column6: Zhège chéngshì dōngtiān yòng méi qǔnuǎn.
column7: This city uses coal for heating in winter.

column3: Gas used for cooking and heating at home, originally made from coal: 煤气灶 "gas stove", 煤气罐 "gas cylinder", 关煤气 "turn off the gas". The word can also mean carbon monoxide: 煤气中毒. In Taiwan household gas is called 瓦斯. 煤 "coal" + 气 "gas, air".
column6: Zuò wán fàn yào guān méiqì.
column7: After cooking you must turn off the gas.

column3: Scissors: 一把剪刀 (measure word 把). 剪 is "to cut with scissors" and 刀 "knife", the simplest word for a blade. In 剪 the 刀 below is the meaning part and 前 on top gives the sound (qián, jiǎn), a weak match. Also 菜刀 "kitchen knife" and 小刀 "small knife".
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī bǎ jiǎndāo.
column7: Please give me a pair of scissors.

column3: Scissors, the spoken word in the north, with the neutral-tone suffix 子; 剪刀 is the more general and written one. Also "shears": 园艺剪子. The same measure word 把 is used: 一把剪子.
column6: Jiǎnzi zài chōuti lǐ.
column7: The scissors are in the drawer.

column3: To cut with scissors: 剪头发 "get a haircut", 剪指甲 "cut nails", 剪纸 "paper cut art". It is also used for video work: 剪辑 "to edit footage", and in the app era "剪视频". The 刀 below shows the tool. Usually in a verb phrase with an object.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng qù jiǎn tóufa.
column7: I want to go and get a haircut.

column3: Glue in liquid form: 用胶水粘 "stick with glue", 一瓶胶水. 胶 means "sticky stuff, glue, rubber" and 水 "liquid". The flesh radical ⺼ and 交 "to join" suggest tissue that connects. Related words are 胶带 "tape" and 橡胶 "rubber".
column4: 用胶水把纸贴在本子上。
column5: 用膠水把紙貼在本子上。
column6: Yòng jiāoshuǐ bǎ zhǐ tiē zài běnzi shàng.
column7: Stick the paper onto the notebook with glue.

column3: Adhesive tape: 透明胶带 "clear tape", 一卷胶带 (measure word 卷 "roll"). It is also magnetic tape, as in a cassette. 带 is a "belt, strip" and appears in 领带 "necktie", 地带 "zone" and 带 "to bring".
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī juǎn jiāodài.
column7: Please give me a roll of tape.

column3: Fountain pen, literally "steel pen": 钢 "steel" + 笔 "pen". Typical: 用钢笔写字, 一支钢笔, 钢笔字. 钢 has the metal radical 钅 and 冈 as sound, which really is gāng. In 笔, bamboo ⺮ and 毛 "hair" are the old brush: a bamboo rod with a hairy tip.
column6: Yéye xǐhuan yòng gāngbǐ xiězì.
column7: Grandfather likes to write with a fountain pen.

column3: A writing brush, for calligraphy and ink painting: 毛笔字 "brush-written characters", 用毛笔练字 "practice with a brush". 毛 "hair" + 笔 "pen". Measure word 支. It is the old writing tool, and the 笔 character is itself a picture of one: bamboo with hair on the end.
column6: Tā měitiān yòng máobǐ liànzì.
column7: He practices calligraphy with a brush every day.

column3: A lock (一把锁) and "to lock" (锁门 "lock the door", 锁上). Both noun and verb. The metal radical 钅 on the left shows the material; the right part is a simplified form of the original and no longer clearly shows the sound. Typical: 忘了锁门, 锁在家里.
column6: Chūmén qián bié wàng le suǒ mén.
column7: Don't forget to lock the door before you go out.

column3: A fan for cooling: 一把扇子, 摇扇子 "wave a fan", 折扇 "folding fan". 扇 shows a door 户 above feathers 羽, since early fans were made of feathers. The neutral 子 follows. Electric fans are 电风扇 or 风扇.
column6: Xiàtiān tā ná zhe yī bǎ shànzi.
column7: In summer she holds a fan.

column3: As a measure word, shàn for doors, windows, screens and gates: 一扇门 "a door", 一扇窗 "a window". As a noun it is a "fan" (扇子) or the leaf of a door. Read shān in the verb sense, see the next entry. The parts are a door 户 and feathers 羽: a door-like frame made of feathers.
column6: Nà shàn chuānghu kāi zhe.
column7: That window is open.

column3: As a verb, shān, "to fan" and "to slap": 扇风 "fan the air", 扇耳光 "slap someone's face", 扇火 "fan the fire". The reading changes with the sense: shàn is the noun or measure word, shān the verb. Usually with an object or with a tool: 用扇子扇.
column6: Tiān tài rè le, tā yòng shǒu shān fēng.
column7: It was so hot that he fanned himself with his hand.

column3: A battery: 换电池 "change the battery", 电池没电了 "the battery is dead", 充电池 "charge a battery". 电 is "electricity" and 池 "pool", a pool of electric power. The water radical 氵 in 池 shows a pool. 手机电池 is a phone battery.
column6: Shǒujī diànchí méi diàn le.
column7: The phone battery is dead.

column3: A small bell, for a bicycle, a door, a school: 上课铃 "class bell", 自行车铃. The metal radical 钅 shows a metal object and 令 gives the sound. As a word on its own it is seen in phrases like 铃响了 "the bell rang"; in many words it is paired with other characters, like 门铃 "doorbell" and 铃声.
column4: 铃响了，同学们回到教室。
column5: 鈴響了，同學們回到教室。
column6: Líng xiǎng le, tóngxuémen huídào jiàoshì.
column7: The bell rang and the students went back to the classroom.

column3: Ring, the sound of a bell, on a phone or a school bell: 手机铃声 "phone ringtone", 铃声响了 "the bell rang". Made from 铃 "bell" + 声 "sound". 声 is read shēng in the first tone, not neutral. Typical verbs: 响 "ring", 设置铃声 "set a ringtone".
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī língshēng tài chǎo le.
column7: My phone's ringtone is too loud.

column3: A (Western-style) suit: 西 "west" + 装 "clothes, outfit". Typical: 穿西装, 一套西装 (measure word 套 for a suit), 西装革履 "suit and leather shoes", said of a smartly dressed man. 装 has 衣 "clothes" below and 壮 on top for sound. Worn to job interviews and weddings; Chinese-style clothing is 中山装 or 唐装.
column6: Tā chuān zhe xīzhuāng qù miànshì.
column7: He went to the interview in a suit.

column3: Jeans: 牛仔 is "cowboy" (牛 "ox" + 仔 "young person"), then 裤 "trousers". Measure word 条 as for any trousers: 一条牛仔裤. 裤 is 衤 (clothes) + 库, which is simply a sound part; the same 衤 begins 衣服's family such as 衬衫 and 裙子. Also 牛仔裙 "denim skirt".
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī tiáo niúzǎikù.
column7: I want to buy a pair of jeans.

column3: Down jacket, the padded winter coat: 羽 "feather" + 绒 "soft fine hair, down" + 服 "clothing". Measure word 件: 一件羽绒服. Both 羽 (two feathers) and 绒 (with 纟 "silk") fit the idea of soft stuff. 服 is "clothes" in 衣服 and 西服, and also means "to serve".
column6: Dōngtiān wǒ chuān yǔróngfú.
column7: In winter I wear a down jacket.

column3: High-heeled shoes: 高 "high" + 跟 "heel" + 鞋 "shoe". Measure word 双 for a pair: 一双高跟鞋. 跟 has 足 "foot" on the left and 艮 as sound, and is related to 根 "root", so the heel is the "root" of the foot. 跟 also means "with" and "to follow". 鞋 has the leather radical 革.
column6: Tā bù xíguàn chuān gāogēnxié.
column7: She is not used to wearing high heels.

column3: Leather shoes, formal shoes as opposed to 运动鞋 "sports shoes": 穿皮鞋, 擦皮鞋 "polish shoes", 一双皮鞋. 皮 is "skin, leather" and 鞋 "shoe" with the leather radical 革. 皮 was drawn as a hand stripping the hide off an animal.
column6: Bàba měitiān zǎoshang cā píxié.
column7: Dad polishes his leather shoes every morning.

column3: Necktie: 打领带 or 系领带 "wear a tie", 一条领带. 领 means "collar, neck" (令 for sound, 页 "head" as meaning, because the neck is by the head) and 带 is a "band, belt". The same 领 is in 领导 "leader" and 衣领 "collar". Worn with 西装.
column4: 他打了一条蓝色的领带。
column5: 他打了一條藍色的領帶。
column6: Tā dǎ le yī tiáo lánsè de lǐngdài.
column7: He wore a blue tie.

column3: To drape over the shoulders, to wrap around a coat or scarf without putting the arms in: 披着外套, 披上, 披肩 "shawl". Also in 披头发 "have loose hair". The hand radical 扌 shows the action and 皮 "skin, fur" the sound and the idea of fur put on the shoulders. It also means "to open, to split", seen in written phrases.
column6: Tā jiān shàng pī zhe yī tiáo wéijīn.
column7: She has a scarf draped over her shoulders.

column3: A backpack, rucksack: 背 here is bēi, "to carry on the back", and 包 "bag", so a 背包 is a bag carried on the back. The word is also a verb, "to go backpacking" (背包旅行). The noun 背 "back" is read bèi in the fourth tone. Measure word 个 or 只: 一个背包. 包 is a swaddled baby, a 巳 inside the wrapping 勹.
column6: Wǒ de bēibāo lǐ yǒu yī píng shuǐ.
column7: There is a bottle of water in my backpack.

column3: To dress up, to make oneself up, also "style of dress": 打扮得很漂亮 "dressed up beautifully", 精心打扮 "dress carefully", 打扮成… "dress up as…". The second syllable is neutral. Both characters have the hand radical 扌; 扮 also means "to play a role" in 扮演.
column6: Tā jīntiān dǎban de hěn piàoliang.
column7: She is dressed up beautifully today.

column3: Ugly, and also "shameful": 丑闻 "scandal", 丑八怪 "ugly person". The traditional form of this meaning is 醜; simplification gave it the character 丑, which already existed as the 2nd earthly branch (the ox year) and as the "clown" role in Chinese opera. So the same character is read chǒu in all of these. The opposite of "ugly" is 美 or 漂亮.
column6: Zhè zhī gǒu kàn qǐlái hěn chǒu.
column7: This dog looks ugly.

column3: Charming, captivating: 迷人的笑容 "a charming smile", 迷人的风景 "enchanting scenery". 迷 is "to be lost, to be fascinated" and 人 "person": something that "makes people lost". 迷 has the walking radical 辶 and 米 for the sound, which still rhymes with mí. Used for a person's smile, voice, eyes and for a place.
column6: Tā de xiàoróng hěn mírén.
column7: Her smile is very charming.

column3: Look, appearance: 她小时候的模样 "how she looked as a child". Note that 模 is read mú here, not mó as in 模型 "model". A spoken word, often about a face or figure: 长得什么模样 "what does he look like". Also "about, roughly" in 三十岁模样, "around thirty years old".
column4: 孩子们长大了，都变了模样。
column5: 孩子們長大了，都變了模樣。
column6: Háizimen zhǎngdà le, dōu biàn le múyàng.
column7: The children have grown up and all look different.

column3: Appearance, look, face, written or formal: 城市面貌 "the look of a city", 精神面貌 "mental outlook", 面貌一新 "take on a new look". For a person's face, 面貌 is the face and features; for places and conditions it is the overall appearance. 面 is a face drawn with an eye; 貌 has the beast radical 豸 and 皃 "looks".
column4: 这座城市的面貌发生了很大变化。
column5: 這座城市的面貌發生了很大變化。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì de miànmào fāshēng le hěn dà biànhuà.
column7: The look of this city has changed greatly.

column3: Elegant bearing, poise, especially of a man: 很有风度 "have style and grace", 风度翩翩 "gracefully poised". It is about manner and behavior rather than appearance, and always positive. 风 "wind" here means "style, manner", as in 作风 "work style". 度 is a "degree, measure" (温度 "temperature").
column4: 他很有风度，大家都喜欢他。
column5: 他很有風度，大家都喜歡他。
column6: Tā hěn yǒu fēngdù, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan tā.
column7: He has great poise and everybody likes him.

column3: Expression, look on one's face that shows the mind: 神情紧张 "a tense look", 神情严肃 "a serious look". It is more written than 表情 and describes the whole bearing of the face and eyes. 神 is "spirit" with the spirit radical 礻 and 情 "feeling" with the heart radical 忄.
column6: Tā de shénqíng hěn jǐnzhāng.
column7: She looks very tense.

column3: Complexion, used for health: 脸色不好 "look unwell", 脸色苍白 "pale face". It also means the mood on someone's face: 看别人的脸色 "watch other people's moods", 给他脸色看 "give him a cold look". 色 is read sè here, as in all color words.
column4: 你的脸色不太好，是不是生病了？
column5: 你的臉色不太好，是不是生病了？
column6: Nǐ de liǎnsè bù tài hǎo, shì bu shì shēngbìng le?
column7: You don't look well. Are you sick?

column3: Brain, mind, mostly as the thinking power: 脑子好 "bright", 动脑子 "use your head", 没脑子 "brainless". It is the spoken word; the organ in a medical sense is 大脑. The neutral 子 follows. The flesh radical ⺼ on 脑 is also in 脸, 肠 and 胃.
column6: Nǐ dòngdong nǎozi xiǎng yī xiǎng.
column7: Use your head and think about it.

column3: Brain, cerebrum, the organ, in science and health talk: 大脑发育 "brain development", 大脑皮层 "cerebral cortex". In spoken language 脑子 is the usual word.
column6: Shuìmián duì dànǎo hěn zhòngyào.
column7: Sleep is important for the brain.

column3: Intestines. Usually in compounds: 大肠 "large intestine", 小肠 "small intestine", 肠胃 "stomach and bowels", and 香肠 "sausage". The same 肠 appears in the idiom 肠子都悔青了 "regret bitterly".
column6: Shíwù zài xiǎocháng lǐ bèi xīshōu.
column7: Food is absorbed in the small intestine.

column3: Gall bladder and, far more often, "courage, guts": 胆大 "bold", 胆小 "timid", 胆子 "courage" (大胆 "daring"). The idiom for a coward is 胆小鬼. The flesh radical ⺼ shows a body part and 旦 gives the sound dàn, close to dǎn.
column4: 他胆很小，不敢一个人睡。
column5: 他膽很小，不敢一個人睡。
column6: Tā dǎn hěn xiǎo, bù gǎn yī gè rén shuì.
column7: He is timid and does not dare sleep alone.

column3: Stomach: 胃疼 "stomachache", 胃口 "appetite", 胃病 "stomach trouble". The picture is a stomach 月 (flesh) with food 田 inside it. In speech people say 我的胃不舒服 where English says "stomach". Do not use it for the belly on the outside, which is 肚子.
column6: Wǒ de wèi yǒudiǎnr téng.
column7: My stomach hurts a little.

column3: Shoulder, and as a verb "to shoulder" a duty: 肩上, 双肩, 肩负责任 "bear responsibility". The everyday spoken word for the shoulder is 肩膀. The character shows a door 户 over flesh ⺼. Often with 背 "carry on the back" or 扛 "carry on the shoulder".
column6: Tā jiān shàng bēi zhe yī gè dà bāo.
column7: He carries a big bag on his shoulder.

column3: Muscle: 练肌肉 "build muscle", 肌肉发达 "well-muscled", 肌肉酸痛 "sore muscles". 肌 is "muscle" and 肉 "flesh". Both carry the flesh radical, 肉 in its short form ⺼ inside 肌. 肉 alone is "meat" for food; the animal's muscle is the same word.
column4: 他每天去健身房练肌肉。
column5: 他每天去健身房練肌肉。
column6: Tā měitiān qù jiànshēnfáng liàn jīròu.
column7: He goes to the gym every day to build muscle.

column3: Skin: 皮肤白 "fair skin", 皮肤干 "dry skin", 皮肤过敏 "skin allergy". 皮 is a hand stripping hide; 肤 is flesh ⺼ plus 夫 for the sound (fū and fū). Used for human skin and general talk about care and condition; skin of a fruit is 皮.
column6: Dōngtiān wǒ de pífū hěn gān.
column7: My skin is very dry in winter.

column3: Fingernail (or toenail, 脚指甲): 剪指甲 "cut nails", 涂指甲 "paint nails". 指 is "finger, to point" and 甲 "shell, armor": the fingers' shell. The second syllable is usually neutral in speech (zhǐjia). 甲 is also the first of the ten heavenly stems, "A", as in 甲方 "Party A".
column4: 他的指甲太长了，该剪了。
column5: 他的指甲太長了，該剪了。
column6: Tā de zhǐjia tài cháng le, gāi jiǎn le.
column7: His nails are too long and need cutting.

column3: Footstep, pace: 加快脚步 "quicken one's pace", 放慢脚步 "slow down", 脚步声 "the sound of footsteps". It also figures in the sense of "pace of progress": 跟上时代的脚步 "keep up with the times". 脚 "foot" + 步 "step", where 步 is two feet, one in front of the other.
column6: Tā jiākuài le jiǎobù.
column7: He quickened his pace.

column3: Beard, moustache: 留胡子 "grow a beard", 刮胡子 "shave". The traditional form is 鬍子, with the hair radical 髟, while the simplified 胡 is also the character for 胡 "foreign, barbarian" and a common surname. The 子 is neutral. It also means "bandit" colloquially (old-fashioned).
column6: Bàba měitiān zǎoshang guā húzi.
column7: Dad shaves every morning.

column3: Both hands: 用双手 "with both hands". It is polite to give or receive things with both hands: 双手递给他. 双 is "a pair" and in its form is two 又 "hands" side by side; 手 is a hand with the fingers. 双 also counts pairs: 一双手 "a pair of hands", 一双鞋.
column6: Tā yòng shuāngshǒu jiēguò lǐwù.
column7: He took the gift with both hands.

column3: Sweat: 出汗 "sweat", 流汗, 擦汗 "wipe sweat", 满头大汗 "head dripping with sweat". 汗 is also an internet interjection for being at a loss ("sweat!"), like an embarrassed 'ugh'. The water radical 氵 is at the left and 干 gives the sound (gān, hàn).
column6: Tā cā le cā tóu shàng de hàn.
column7: He wiped the sweat from his head.

column3: To sweat: 出汗, 出了一身汗 "break out in a sweat", 容易出汗 "sweat easily". It is a verb plus object, so 了 goes between: 出了很多汗. 出 shows a sprout coming out of a container, "to go out". Compare 流汗, which is more about running down.
column6: Tiān tài rè, wǒ yīzhí chūhàn.
column7: It's so hot that I keep sweating.

column3: Part of the body or a location on something: 身体的各个部位 "every part of the body", 受伤的部位 "the injured spot". 部 is "part" with the place radical 阝 and 位 is "position", from 亻 (person) + 立 "stand". It is a written, precise word, used by doctors and in instructions; for a general "part", 部分 is the word.
column6: Nǐ nǎ ge bùwèi bù shūfu?
column7: Which part of your body feels unwell?

column3: Nerve in anatomy: 神经系统 "nervous system", 神经痛 "nerve pain". Colloquially it also means "mentally unstable, crazy": 神经病 and 你神经啊! are insulting, so avoid them with people you do not know. 神经紧张 "nervous, on edge". 神 is "spirit" and 经 originally the warp threads of cloth, here "channel".
column6: Tā yǒudiǎn shénjīng jǐnzhāng.
column7: He is a bit nervous.

column3: Gaze, look and, in a figure, "attention, vision": 目光敏锐 "sharp-eyed", 目光短浅 "short-sighted", 吸引目光 "attract attention", 目光落在… "eyes fall on…". 目 is the eye turned on its side, 光 "light". A written word; in talk, 眼光 or 眼神 are also used.
column4: 大家的目光都落在她身上。
column5: 大家的目光都落在她身上。
column6: Dàjiā de mùguāng dōu luò zài tā shēnshang.
column7: Everyone's eyes were on her.

column3: Virus, biological or computer: 新冠病毒, 电脑病毒, 感染病毒. Built from 病 "illness" (the sickness radical 疒) + 毒 "poison", so "disease poison". To remove a computer virus you say 杀毒. Typical verbs: 感染 "to infect", 传播 "to spread".
column6: Zhè zhǒng bìngdú chuánbō de hěn kuài.
column7: This virus spreads quickly.

column3: To massage and "massage": 做按摩, 按摩一下肩膀, 足底按摩 "foot massage", 按摩店. 按 is "to press" and 摩 "to rub", both with a hand: 扌 in 按, and 手 inside 摩. The sound parts 安 and 麻 still help: 安 gives àn, 麻 má, mó. 一下 after the verb makes it soft: 按摩一下.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng qù ànmó yīxià jiānbǎng.
column7: I'd like to get my shoulders massaged.

column3: To cough. By itself it is bound; the usual word is 咳嗽 (késou). In 咳嗽 the second syllable is neutral in speech. Typical: 咳嗽得很厉害 "cough badly", 咳嗽药 "cough medicine". The mouth radical 口 shows a sound the mouth makes and 亥 is the sound part.
column6: Wǒ késou de hěn lìhai.
column7: I have a bad cough.

column3: Outpatient service: the part of a hospital where patients are seen without staying overnight, as opposed to 住院 "be admitted". Typical: 看门诊, 门诊部, 门诊大楼, 挂号 "register" before you are seen. 门 is "door" and 诊 "to examine a patient", with the speech radical 讠 because the doctor asks questions.
column4: 她今天上午去医院看门诊。
column5: 她今天上午去醫院看門診。
column6: Tā jīntiān shàngwǔ qù yīyuàn kàn ménzhěn.
column7: This morning she went to the hospital to see the outpatient clinic.

column3: To diagnose and "a diagnosis": 医生诊断他得了肺炎 "the doctor diagnosed pneumonia", 诊断结果 "result of the diagnosis", 误诊 "misdiagnose". Used by doctors and about machines too. 诊 is "to examine" and 断 "to judge, decide, cut", whose traditional 斷 shows grain 米 cut by an axe 斤.
column6: Yīshēng zhěnduàn tā dé le fèiyán.
column7: The doctor diagnosed him with pneumonia.

column3: Traditional Chinese medicine, herbal remedies as opposed to 西药 "Western medicine": 吃中药, 煎中药 "brew herbal medicine", 中药店. Note that 中 is read zhōng here, "Chinese". 药 has the grass radical 艹 on top, as most medicines were plants, and 约 as the sound part.
column6: Zhè wǎn zhōngyào hěn kǔ.
column7: This bowl of herbal medicine is very bitter.

column3: To inject, an injection: 注射疫苗 "inject a vaccine", 注射器 "syringe", 打针 is the everyday word. 注射 is a written, medical word. 注 "to pour" has water 氵 and 主 as sound; 射 is a bow 身 drawn by a hand 寸, "to shoot". So an injection is "pouring + shooting" in.
column6: Hùshi gěi tā zhùshè le yìmiáo.
column7: The nurse gave him a vaccine injection.

column3: To be poisoned: 食物中毒 "food poisoning", 煤气中毒 "gas poisoning". Here 中 is read zhòng, "to hit", like in 中奖 "win a prize" and 打中 "hit the target". The verb 中 means "to be struck by" something unwelcome; the word is 中 + 毒 "poison". It is an intransitive verb: 他中毒了.
column4: 吃了不新鲜的鱼，他中毒了。
column5: 吃了不新鮮的魚，他中毒了。
column6: Chī le bù xīnxiān de yú, tā zhòngdú le.
column7: He ate stale fish and got food poisoning.

column3: Poisonous, toxic: 有毒的蘑菇 "poisonous mushrooms", 有毒气体 "toxic gas", with the opposite 无毒 "non-toxic". Used before a noun with 的, or alone as a predicate: 这种草有毒. Warnings use it: 有毒，请勿食用. It is the plain word for natural or chemical poison.
column6: Zhè zhǒng mógu yǒudú, bié chī.
column7: This mushroom is poisonous, don't eat it.

column3: Harmful: 有害物质 "harmful substances", 对…有害 "harmful to…", the opposite is 有益. It is an adjective that takes 对 for who is harmed: 吸烟对身体有害. A formal word, common in warnings and news. 害 is "harm", also 害怕 "afraid" and 灾害 "disaster".
column6: Xīyān duì shēntǐ yǒuhài.
column7: Smoking is harmful to health.

column3: Poison, toxin and "drugs": 病毒 "virus", 毒品 "narcotics", 吸毒 "take drugs", 中毒, 有毒. As an adjective it means "vicious": 毒蛇 "venomous snake", 心狠手毒 "cruel". Often a short, sharp word in compounds. The 毒 character has 母 "mother" at the bottom as its sound part, which no longer sounds alike.
column6: Zhè zhǒng shé de dú hěn qiáng.
column7: The venom of this snake is very strong.

column3: To kill viruses: the computer sense, 杀毒软件 "antivirus software", 杀毒 as a command. It can also mean "to disinfect" in the physical sense, less often. 杀 "to kill" is the simplified form of 殺, from which one part was dropped; 毒 is "poison", here "virus". Use 病毒 for the virus itself.
column4: 我的电脑装了杀毒软件。
column5: 我的電腦裝了殺毒軟體。
column6: Wǒ de diànnǎo zhuāng le shādú ruǎnjiàn.
column7: I installed antivirus software on my computer.

column3: To disinfect, to sterilize: 消毒水 "disinfectant", 高温消毒 "sterilize with heat", 给手消毒. A verb-object word, so 了 and the object go in between: 消了毒. 消 has water 氵 and 肖 as sound, and means "to put out, to remove" as in 消失 "disappear". So 消毒 is "remove the germs".
column4: 用之前要先把杯子消毒。
column5: 用之前要先把杯子消毒。
column6: Yòng zhīqián yào xiān bǎ bēizi xiāodú.
column7: Disinfect the cup before use.

column3: Allergic, to have an allergy: 对花粉过敏 "allergic to pollen", 过敏反应 "allergic reaction", 皮肤过敏. The pattern is 对 + the thing + 过敏. It also means "oversensitive" in a figure: 他对批评很过敏. 过 is "too much" here and 敏 "quick, sensitive", so literally "too sensitive".
column6: Wǒ duì huāfěn guòmǐn.
column7: I am allergic to pollen.

column3: To maintain, to take care of: 保养汽车 "service a car", 保养皮肤 "care for the skin", 定期保养 "regular maintenance". It is used for machines, and for the body and looks. 保 is a person 亻 with a child (in the old shape, a person carrying a child on the back), "to protect"; 养 is "to raise, nourish".
column6: Qìchē yào dìngqī bǎoyǎng.
column7: A car needs regular servicing.

column3: Sleep, in a more formal or medical way than 睡觉: 睡眠不足 "lack of sleep", 睡眠质量 "sleep quality", 改善睡眠 "improve sleep". It can also mean computer "sleep mode". Both characters have the eye radical 目 on the left, with 垂 and 民 as the sounds: the eyes close and sleep comes.
column6: Tā zuìjìn shuìmián bù hǎo.
column7: He hasn't been sleeping well lately.

column3: Long life, long-lived: 健康长寿 "healthy and long-lived", 长寿面 "longevity noodles" eaten on a birthday. Said as praise or a wish. Here 长 is cháng "long", not zhǎng "to grow". It works as an adjective: 他很长寿. 寿 also means "life span" and "birthday of an elderly person": 祝寿.
column4: 爷爷活到九十岁，真长寿。
column5: 爺爺活到九十歲，真長壽。
column6: Yéye huó dào jiǔshí suì, zhēn chángshòu.
column7: Grandpa lived to ninety, a long life indeed.

column3: Physical strength, stamina: 体力好 "strong", 体力差 "weak", 体力劳动 "manual labor", 恢复体力 "recover one's strength". Compare 力气, which is spoken and about the strength used on a task. 体 is the body (亻 person + 本 "root, base") and 力 is a plough, so "strength".
column6: Pá shān xūyào hěn hǎo de tǐlì.
column7: Climbing mountains takes good stamina.

column3: To spit and "to put out": 吐痰 "spit phlegm", 吐出来 "spit out", 吐舌头 "stick out one's tongue", and figuratively 吐露 "reveal". Here read tǔ, in the third tone; the verb "to vomit" is tù, in the fourth tone. The mouth radical 口 and 土 as sound give both readings the same shape.
column6: Qǐng bùyào suídì tǔ tán.
column7: Please do not spit on the ground.

column3: To vomit: 想吐 "feel sick", 吐了 "threw up", 呕吐 "vomit" (written). This is the fourth tone, tù; the same character in the third tone, tǔ, means "to spit". Typical: 坐车坐得想吐 "carsick", 吃坏了肚子又吐又拉 "vomiting and diarrhea".
column6: Tā zuò chē shí juéde xiǎng tù.
column7: He felt like throwing up in the car.

column3: To give up (a habit): 戒烟 "quit smoking", 戒酒 "quit drinking", 戒网瘾 "break an internet habit". It also means "to warn", as in 戒备 "be on guard", and appears in 戒指 "ring". The shape shows two hands 廾 holding up a halberd 戈 as a warning.
column6: Tā zhōngyú bǎ yān jiè le.
column7: He finally gave up smoking.

column3: Children, sons and daughters, especially when one speaks of parents and children: 儿女双全 "having both sons and daughters", 为儿女操心 "worry about one's children". It is a warm, slightly literary word; in daily speech 孩子 is more common. 儿女情长 describes young lovers' tenderness.
column4: 他的儿女都在国外工作。
column5: 他的兒女都在國外工作。
column6: Tā de érnǚ dōu zài guówài gōngzuò.
column7: His children all work abroad.

column3: Generation and "lifetime", the group of one's age in a family: 长辈 "elder", 晚辈 "younger people", 前辈 "senior, those who came before", 一辈子 "all one's life". It is a bound character, mostly seen in these compounds. 辈 has 车 "cart" as the meaning part, in the traditional form 輩, a line of carts, and 非 for sound.
column6: Duì zhǎngbèi yào yǒu lǐmào.
column7: You should be polite to your elders.

column3: All one's life, a lifetime: 一辈子的朋友 "friends for life", 一辈子都… "for one's whole life". Spoken. It goes before the verb as a time expression, often with 都 or 也 and a negative to stress "never": 一辈子也忘不了. 辈 means "generation", and 子 is the neutral-tone suffix.
column4: 我一辈子都不会忘记你。
column5: 我一輩子都不會忘記你。
column6: Wǒ yībèizi dōu bù huì wàngjì nǐ.
column7: I will never forget you as long as I live.

column3: Age, number of years of a person: 年龄大 "old", 年龄小 "young", 年龄限制 "age limit", 年龄段 "age group". It is neutral and general; asking someone's age uses 多大 or 几岁, not 年龄. 龄 has the teeth radical 齿, as ages of animals were told from their teeth, and 令 as the sound, as in 铃 and 领.
column6: Zhège yóuxì yǒu niánlíng xiànzhì.
column7: This game has an age limit.

column3: Oneself, in person: it refers to the person concerned: 本人到场 "appear in person", 我本人 "I myself", 他本人 "he himself". In formal speech and forms it also means "I": 本人认为…. The sense is "the very person", and it is placed after the pronoun or noun it stresses.
column6: Bàn zhè jiàn shì bìxū běnrén qù.
column7: You must go in person to handle this.

column3: Everybody, all of us, a friendly spoken word, mostly in the north: 大伙儿都来了 "everyone has come". It is used to address a group one belongs to or is friendly with: 大伙儿听我说. The erhua ending 儿 is part of the word. Traditional 大伙兒 keeps 伙 as in the simplified form, as the other form is 夥.
column6: Dàhuǒr yīqǐ lái bāngmáng ba.
column7: Let's all help together.

column3: Male, men: a neutral or formal word for the male sex, used in statistics, medicine and ads: 男性朋友, 男性员工, 男性用品 "men's goods". 性 here is a suffix meaning "gender/nature", as in 女性 and 个性. 男 is a field 田 and strength 力: the man who does the field work.
column4: 这家公司的男性员工比较多。
column5: 這家公司的男性員工比較多。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de nánxìng yuángōng bǐjiào duō.
column7: This company has more male employees.

column3: Woman, women, female: the polite, general term, used where 女人 sounds blunt: 女性朋友, 现代女性, 女性用品. The adjective-like use before a noun is common. With 性 "gender" as the suffix and 女 "woman" drawn as a figure with folded arms. 女士 is a polite title.
column4: 现代女性的工作压力很大。
column5: 現代女性的工作壓力很大。
column6: Xiàndài nǚxìng de gōngzuò yālì hěn dà.
column7: Modern women are under a lot of pressure at work.

column3: A person, a figure of a certain kind: 知名人士 "a well-known figure", 专业人士 "professionals", 各界人士 "people from all circles", 爱国人士. It always comes with a modifier and is used in news and formal writing. The 士 is an old ax shape that came to mean "scholar" and then "person of a certain standing".
column4: 参加会议的有各界人士。
column5: 參加會議的有各界人士。
column6: Cānjiā huìyì de yǒu gèjiè rénshì.
column7: People from all walks of life attended the meeting.

column3: Person, figure of importance, and "character" in a story: 重要人物 "an important figure", 历史人物 "historical figure", 小人物 "a nobody", 小说里的人物 "characters in a novel". 物 is "thing", so literally "people and things", used for a notable person.
column4: 他是这个领域的重要人物。
column5: 他是這個領域的重要人物。
column6: Tā shì zhège lǐngyù de zhòngyào rénwù.
column7: He is an important figure in this field.

column3: Citizens, the people of a nation: 国民经济 "national economy", 国民收入 "national income", 国民素质 "the quality of a nation's people". It is formal and political. 国 shows a treasure 玉 inside a border 囗 and 民 means "the people". Compare 公民, which stresses civic rights.
column4: 国民的生活水平提高了。
column5: 國民的生活水平提高了。
column6: Guómín de shēnghuó shuǐpíng tígāo le.
column7: The living standard of the people has risen.

column3: The masses, the public: 广大群众 "the broad masses", 群众的意见 "the people's opinion", 群众路线. The word is common in official and political language on the mainland. In everyday life, 大家 or 人们 are used. 群 has a sheep radical 羊 (a herd) and 众 is three people 人, "a crowd" (traditional 眾).
column6: Tā hěn liǎojiě qúnzhòng de xūyào.
column7: He understands well what the people need.

column3: A genius and "genius, brilliant": 他是个天才, 天才儿童 "gifted child", 音乐天才. 天 "heaven" + 才 "talent": a gift from heaven. It goes before a noun like an adjective or is a noun on its own. Not to be confused with 人才 "a talented person who is made through effort".
column4: 这个孩子是个音乐天才。
column5: 這個孩子是個音樂天才。
column6: Zhège háizi shì ge yīnyuè tiāncái.
column7: This child is a musical genius.

column3: Idol, someone admired, mostly a singer, actor or athlete: 我的偶像, 偶像剧 "idol drama", 偶像歌手, 追星 "follow a star". It can also mean an idol statue to be worshiped, in its first sense. 偶 is "image, a figure" and 像 "likeness".
column6: Tā de ǒuxiàng shì yī wèi gēshǒu.
column7: Her idol is a singer.

column3: Neighbor: 我的邻居, 邻居家 "the neighbor's home", 做邻居 "be neighbors". It refers to those who live next door or nearby. 邻 has the place radical 阝 (in this form a "town") and 居 means "to live, to dwell", also in 居住 and 住居. 隔壁 often refers to the next-door home or neighbor.
column6: Wǒ de línjū shì yī wèi lǎoshī.
column7: My neighbor is a teacher.

column3: Lifelong, for life: 终身学习 "lifelong learning", 终身大事 "the big event of a lifetime", meaning marriage, 终身难忘 "unforgettable for life". It is a formal modifier placed before a noun. 终 "end" + 身 "body, life", so "to one's body's end". Compare 一辈子, which is spoken.
column4: 我们要养成终身学习的习惯。
column5: 我們要養成終身學習的習慣。
column6: Wǒmen yào yǎngchéng zhōngshēn xuéxí de xíguàn.
column7: We should develop the habit of lifelong learning.

column3: Elephant, the full word for the animal: 一头大象 (measure word 头), 大象的鼻子 "the elephant's trunk". 象 alone is a bound character and the picture of an elephant: the top shows the trunk and the rest the head and body. 象 turns up in 印象 "impression", 现象 "phenomenon" and 形象 "image".
column6: Dàxiàng de bízi hěn cháng.
column7: The elephant's trunk is very long.

column3: Giant panda, often shortened to 熊猫. It is literally "big bear-cat", and the national treasure of China (国宝), mostly found in Sichuan. 熊 "bear" and 猫 "cat" share the animal radical 犭 on 猫; the sound part 苗 of 猫 still sounds close (miáo, māo). Measure word 只: 一只大熊猫.
column6: Dàxióngmāo xǐhuan chī zhúzi.
column7: Giant pandas like to eat bamboo.

column3: Bear: 一头熊, 北极熊 "polar bear", 熊猫. In spoken Chinese it is also an insult: "weak, cowardly", 熊样 "pathetic look", 你真熊! and a verb, 熊人 "to scold someone harshly". The foot of the character has 灬, usually "fire" but here an animal's feet in a changed shape.
column6: Dōngtiān, xióng huì zài dòng lǐ shuìjiào.
column7: In winter bears sleep in caves.

column3: Monkey, which is common as the animal and as one of the twelve zodiac signs: 属猴 "born in the year of the monkey". The animal is usually called 猴子. The left part 犭 is the animal radical, and the right 侯 gives the sound, hóu, exactly. A lively child is called a 猴 too: 淘气的小猴.
column6: Tā shǔ hóu, jīnnián èrshísì suì.
column7: He was born in the year of the monkey and is twenty-four.

column3: Tiger: 老虎 is the full word and 虎 is used in zodiac and set phrases: 属虎, 虎年, 虎口 "tiger's mouth", 马马虎虎 "so-so". It also appears in the idiom 虎头蛇尾 "a strong start and a weak end". The top 虍 is the tiger's head, and the lower part its body and legs.
column6: Wǒ shǔ hǔ, nǐ shǔ shénme?
column7: I was born in the year of the tiger. What about you?

column3: Rat, mouse, mostly in compounds: 老鼠 "mouse, rat", 鼠标 "computer mouse", 鼠年. As a bound form it is seldom used alone except in the zodiac, 属鼠. The picture shows a mouse with its paws and tail. The mouse is the first of the twelve zodiac animals.
column6: Māo zài zhuī yī zhī lǎoshǔ.
column7: The cat is chasing a mouse.

column3: Rabbit: the animal is called 兔子 in speech; 兔 alone appears in the zodiac (属兔, 兔年) and fixed words such as 野兔 "hare". A sentence needs 兔子: 一只兔子. Be careful with the tone, tù, fourth. It is a picture of a rabbit with short tail at the lower right.
column6: Tùzi xǐhuan chī húluóbo.
column7: Rabbits like to eat carrots.

column3: Snake: 一条蛇, 毒蛇 "poisonous snake", 蛇年 and the zodiac sign 属蛇. The left part 虫 is the insect/worm radical, which is used for small creeping animals. The right part 它 was originally itself the picture of a snake, and became a pronoun for "it", so 蛇 is the 'snake' again with the radical added.
column6: Cǎocóng lǐ yǒu yī tiáo shé.
column7: There is a snake in the grass.

column3: Duck: 一只鸭子, 烤鸭 "roast duck", 鸭蛋 "duck egg". The 子 is a neutral-tone suffix and 鸭 alone is bound. 鸭 has the bird radical 鸟 and 甲, whose sound (jiǎ) no longer matches yā. The word is used in the idiom 赶鸭子上架 "to push someone into a job they cannot do".
column6: Chítáng lǐ yǒu jǐ zhī yāzi.
column7: There are some ducks in the pond.

column3: Bamboo, the plant: 一根竹子, 竹子做的筷子 "chopsticks made of bamboo". The character 竹 is a picture of two bamboo stalks with leaves, and as a radical (⺮) it sits on top of many things made of bamboo, like 笔 and 筷. Bamboo stands for uprightness. Pandas eat it.
column6: Xióngmāo měitiān chī hěn duō zhúzi.
column7: Pandas eat a lot of bamboo every day.

column3: Peach blossom: 桃花开了 "the peach trees are in bloom", the sign of spring. It is also a figure for love: 桃花运 "luck in romance", 烂桃花 "bad romantic entanglements". 花 as a flower has the grass radical 艹 on top and 化 as the sound, and also means "to spend" (花钱) in other uses.
column4: 春天，公园里的桃花开了。
column5: 春天，公園裡的桃花開了。
column6: Chūntiān, gōngyuán lǐ de táohuā kāi le.
column7: In spring the peach blossoms in the park are out.

column3: Peach tree: 一棵桃树 (measure word 棵 for trees). 桃 "peach" + 树 "tree". 树 has 木 "tree" and the sound part 对 in the simplified form, a stand-in for the traditional 樹. Related: 苹果树 "apple tree", 桃树 and 桃花.
column6: Yuànzi lǐ zhòng zhe yī kē táoshù.
column7: A peach tree is planted in the yard.

column3: Fossil: 恐龙化石 "dinosaur fossil", 古生物化石, 化石燃料 "fossil fuel". 化 is "to change" and 石 "stone", so it is "changed to stone". 化 appears in a long line of words as a suffix meaning "-ize" or "change", such as 现代化, 变化, 文化. 石 shows a rock at the foot of a cliff.
column4: 博物馆里有一块恐龙化石。
column5: 博物館裡有一塊恐龍化石。
column6: Bówùguǎn lǐ yǒu yī kuài kǒnglóng huàshí.
column7: There is a dinosaur fossil in the museum.

column3: To evolve, evolution: 生物进化 "biological evolution", 进化论 "theory of evolution". It is used for living things and also for technology and systems. 进 "to advance" + 化 "to change". 进 is the simplified form of 進, with 井 in place of 隹. The result of the change is often given with 成: 进化成….
column6: Shēngwù bùduàn de jìnhuà.
column7: Living things keep evolving.

column3: Bank, shore, coast: 河岸 "river bank", 海岸 "seashore", 上岸 "go ashore", 靠岸 "come alongside". A written word, mostly in compounds and with verbs of landing. The mountain 山 on top and the cliff 厂 show a steep edge of land; 干 below is the sound part, with the vowel -an, but a different tone.
column6: Chuán kào àn le.
column7: The boat has reached the shore.

column3: On the shore, on land: opposite 水里 or 船上. Typical: 站在岸上 "stand on the bank", 岸上的人. It places something on land as seen from water. 上 here is neutral in the second syllable, ànshang. It is built from 岸 + 上, where 上 is a short stroke above a long one, the opposite of 下.
column6: Rénmen zhàn zài ànshang kàn chuán.
column7: People stand on the bank and watch the boats.

column3: Grassland, prairie: 内蒙古大草原 "the Inner Mongolian steppe", 草原上的牧民 "herders on the grassland". 草 "grass" + 原 "plain". 原 shows a spring 泉 from a cliff 厂, with the sense "source, origin", and then "plain" in the sense of wide open land, so it also appears in 平原 and 高原.
column6: Cǎoyuán shàng yǒu hěn duō niú hé yáng.
column7: There are many cows and sheep on the grassland.

column3: Desert: 撒哈拉沙漠 "the Sahara", 沙漠里没有水. 沙 is "sand" (water and a few dots, grains on a shore) and 漠 is a word for "empty, desolate" with the water radical 氵; here the water radical hints at the lack of it. 漠 appears in 冷漠 "indifferent".
column6: Shāmò lǐ hěn nán zhǎodào shuǐ.
column7: It is hard to find water in the desert.

column3: Plateau: 青藏高原 "the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau", 高原反应 "altitude sickness". 高 "high" + 原 "plain, flat land", i.e. "a high plain". 高 is a picture of a tall building. Typical: 上高原, 在高原上; the word is also used for geography lessons.
column4: 西藏位于世界上最高的高原。
column5: 西藏位於世界上最高的高原。
column6: Xīzàng wèiyú shìjiè shàng zuì gāo de gāoyuán.
column7: Tibet lies on the highest plateau in the world.

column3: Plain: a wide stretch of flat land. 华北平原 "the North China Plain", 一望无际的平原 "a plain as far as the eye can see". 平 is "flat, level" and 原 "open land". Opposite: 山区 or 山地. Most of China's farmland lies on plains.
column6: Zhèlǐ shì yī piàn dà píngyuán.
column7: This is a big plain.

column3: Mountain area, hilly region: 山区的孩子 "children from the mountains", 偏远山区 "remote mountain areas". It often appears in news about poverty, roads or tourism. 山 is a picture of three peaks; 区 is the simplified form of 區, "area, district", which also forms 郊区, 社区 and 地区.
column6: Shānqū de dōngtiān hěn lěng.
column7: Winters in the mountains are cold.

column3: Spring (of water): 泉水 "spring water", 温泉 "hot spring", 山泉 "mountain spring". It is a written, bound-type word and nearly always in compounds, but 一眼泉 "a spring" works alone. In the character, 白 (a spring mouth) sits above 水 "water". The same 泉 is inside 原 as "source".
column6: Shānjiǎo xià yǒu yī yǎn quán.
column7: There is a spring at the foot of the mountain.

column3: Ditch, gully, groove: 水沟 "drain", 沟里 "in the ditch", 山沟 "mountain gully". The figure 沟通 "to communicate" and 代沟 "generation gap" come from it. 氵 shows water; 勾 gives the sound gōu, exactly.
column6: Lùbiān yǒu yī tiáo xiǎo gōu.
column7: There is a small ditch by the road.

column3: Zone, belt, area: 危险地带 "danger zone", 沿海地带 "coastal area", 缓冲地带 "buffer zone". It often has a modifier in front. 地 "land" with 土 and 也 for the sound, and 带 "belt, band". The idea: a strip of land.
column4: 这是一个危险地带，请小心。
column5: 這是一個危險地帶，請小心。
column6: Zhè shì yī gè wēixiǎn dìdài, qǐng xiǎoxīn.
column7: This is a danger zone, please be careful.

column3: Terrain, topography: 地形复杂 "complicated terrain", 地形图 "topographic map", 熟悉地形. 地 "land" + 形 "shape". It describes the shape of the ground, mountains, plains, hills; for the weather, use 天气. 形 "shape" also forms 形状 "shape" and 情形 "situation".
column6: Zhèlǐ de dìxíng hěn fùzá.
column7: The terrain here is very complex.

column3: Reservoir: a lake made by a dam for water supply, irrigation or power. 修水库 "build a reservoir", 水库大坝. 库 is "storehouse" and shows a building 广 with a cart 车 inside; 水库 is a "water storehouse". The same 库 forms 仓库 "warehouse", 车库 "garage" and 数据库 "database".
column6: Zhège shuǐkù wèi quán chéng gōngshuǐ.
column7: This reservoir supplies water to the whole city.

column3: The North Pole, the Arctic: 北极熊 "polar bear", 北极圈 "Arctic Circle". 北 is "north" and 极 "extreme, end", the north extreme. 北 is a picture of two people back to back, which first meant "back" and then was borrowed for "north"; 背 "back" has 北 on top for that reason. Also 极了 after an adjective means "extremely".
column6: Běijí de dōngtiān fēicháng lěng.
column7: Winters in the Arctic are extremely cold.

column3: The South Pole, Antarctica: 南极洲 "the continent of Antarctica", 去南极考察 "go on an expedition to Antarctica". 南 "south" + 极 "extreme". The old picture for 南 was a musical bell, borrowed for the direction. Penguins live at the South Pole, polar bears at the North Pole.
column6: Qǐ'é shēnghuó zài nánjí.
column7: Penguins live in the Antarctic.

column3: Border, frontier region: 边境线 "border line", 边境地区, 守卫边境, 边境贸易. It refers to the zone along the border, not the line itself. 边 is "side, edge" (with 辶, in the simplified form) and 境 is "territory, state" with 土 earth. Used in the news about customs, trade and security.
column4: 两国的边境已经关闭了。
column5: 兩國的邊境已經關閉了。
column6: Liǎng guó de biānjìng yǐjīng guānbì le.
column7: The border between the two countries has been closed.

column3: Area, region, zone: 这个区域, 不同区域 "different regions", 区域经济 "regional economy", 禁止区域. A somewhat formal word for a defined part of a space, a country or a field. 区 is "district" and 域 means "region", with earth 土 on the left and 或 as the sound part, as in 国 in older writing.
column6: Zhège qūyù jìnzhǐ tíngchē.
column7: Parking is forbidden in this area.

column3: Both banks of a river, and "both sides of the Strait", Taiwan and the mainland: 河的两岸, 海峡两岸. In news 两岸关系 "cross-strait relations" is the usual phrase. 两 is "two", a pair as in 两边, and 岸 "shore".
column6: Hé de liǎng'àn dōu shì lǜshù.
column7: Both banks of the river are lined with green trees.

column3: North and south or "north to south": 南北方向 "north-south direction", 南北差异 "the difference between north and south", 走南闯北 "travel everywhere". The order is south-north in Chinese, the reverse of English. It is also the sense of the whole length: 南北长. 南 once pictured a bell, 北 two people back to back.
column6: Zhè tiáo lù shì nánběi fāngxiàng de.
column7: This road runs north to south.

column3: Hole, cave: 山洞 "cave", 洞口 "the mouth of a cave", 老鼠洞 "mouse hole", 黑洞 "black hole". As a counted thing: 一个洞. It also stands for "zero" in speech when numbers are read out, to avoid confusion with 一 (yāo and dòng): 洞洞. The water radical 氵 and 同 as sound give the dòng reading.
column6: Wàzi shàng yǒu yī gè dòng.
column7: There is a hole in the sock.

column3: Rainwater and "rainfall, rain": 雨水充足 "plenty of rain", 雨水少 "little rain", 收集雨水 "collect rainwater". It is a farming and weather word more than 下雨, which is the verb "to rain". 雨水 is also the name of the second solar term in February, "Rain Water". 雨 is a cloud with drops falling.
column6: Jīnnián de yǔshuǐ hěn chōngzú.
column7: There has been plenty of rain this year.

column3: Weather conditions and "meteorology": 气象部门 "the weather bureau", 气象预报 "weather forecast", 气象台 "weather station". In a wider sense it means "atmosphere, scene": 新气象 "a new look", 气象万千 "a scene of great variety". 气 is "air" and 象 "appearance, sign".
column4: 气象部门预报明天有大雨。
column5: 氣象部門預報明天有大雨。
column6: Qìxiàng bùmén yùbào míngtiān yǒu dàyǔ.
column7: The weather bureau forecasts heavy rain for tomorrow.

column3: Sunny and cloudless: 天气晴朗 "the weather is fine", 晴朗的天空 "a clear sky". It describes sky and weather only, not a person's mood (use 开朗 for a cheerful nature). 晴 has the sun 日 and 青 as the sound, still close in qíng, qīng; 朗 has the moon 月 and 良 for the sound, and means "bright".
column4: 今天天气晴朗，适合爬山。
column5: 今天天氣晴朗，適合爬山。
column6: Jīntiān tiānqì qínglǎng, shìhé pá shān.
column7: The weather is clear today, good for climbing a mountain.

column3: Warm, and "to warm up": 暖和 is the spoken adjective and 暖 alone is used in short phrases and compounds, such as 天气暖了, 暖手 "warm one's hands" and 暖气 "central heating". It is softer than 热 "hot". The sun radical 日 on the left shows warmth from the sun, and 爰 gives the sound.
column6: Chūntiān lái le, tiānqì nuǎn le.
column7: Spring has come and the weather is warm.

column3: High temperature: 高温天气 "hot weather", 高温预警 "heat warning", 高温消毒 "sterilize with heat". In weather reports it means unusual heat, about 35 degrees or more. Opposite: 低温. 温 is the simplified form of 溫, shortened on the right, with water 氵 on the left; it is also in 温度 "temperature".
column6: Xiàtiān cháng yǒu gāowēn tiānqì.
column7: In summer there are often very hot days.

column3: In the sky, in the air: 在空中飞 "fly in the air", 空中交通, 空中楼阁 "castles in the air". 空 is "empty, sky" and shows a cave 穴 with the sound part 工 (gōng, kōng), a hollow; the sky is the great hollow. Read kōng in the first tone here, not the fourth (kòng, "free time").
column6: Yī zhī niǎo zài kōngzhōng fēi.
column7: A bird is flying in the air.

column3: The moon as a body in space, in science, news and travel: 登上月球 "land on the moon", 月球表面 "the lunar surface". In everyday speech and poetry the moon is 月亮. 月 "moon" + 球 "ball, sphere": the "moon ball". 球 has the jade radical 王 on the left and 求 for the sound.
column4: 他梦想有一天能去月球。
column5: 他夢想有一天能去月球。
column6: Tā mèngxiǎng yǒu yī tiān néng qù yuèqiú.
column7: He dreams of going to the moon one day.

column3: Outer space: 太空旅行 "space travel", 进入太空 "enter space", 太空站 "space station". 太 "very big" (a 大 with a dot) + 空 "sky". Taiwan uses 太空人 for astronaut; the mainland says 宇航员 or 航天员. Slightly more everyday than 宇宙, which is "the universe".
column4: 宇航员在太空工作了半年。
column5: 宇航員在太空工作了半年。
column6: Yǔhángyuán zài tàikōng gōngzuò le bàn nián.
column7: The astronaut worked in space for half a year.

column3: Satellite, artificial or natural: 人造卫星 "artificial satellite", 卫星电视, 卫星定位 "satellite positioning". In astronomy a moon is also 卫星. 星 "star" has the sun 日 over the sound part 生.
column6: Zhè kē wèixīng rào zhe dìqiú zhuàn.
column7: This satellite goes around the Earth.

column3: Astronomy: 天文学 "the science of astronomy", 天文台 "observatory", 天文望远镜 "telescope", and 天文数字 "an astronomical figure". 天 "sky" + 文, which originally meant a pattern or marking (a tattooed chest), so 天文 is the "patterns of the sky". It is a field of study, not the weather.
column6: Tā duì tiānwén hěn gǎn xìngqù.
column7: He is very interested in astronomy.

column3: Light as it falls on things, "lighting": 光线好 "well lit", 光线暗 "dim", 光线太强. It is about the quantity of light in a place or for a photo, whereas 光 is light in general. 线 means "line, thread" and its silk radical 纟 shows a thread, so 光线 is a "thread of light", a ray.
column6: Zhège fángjiān guāngxiàn hěn hǎo.
column7: This room has good light.

column3: Gray, ash gray, and in figures, "gloomy" or "ambiguous": 灰色的天空 "a gray sky", 灰色心情 "a gloomy mood", 灰色地带 "a gray area". 灰 is a hand 又 over fire 火, the thing left by a fire: "ash". Before a noun, add 的 (灰色的外套) or use 灰 alone (灰外套).
column4: 天空是灰色的，好像要下雨。
column5: 天空是灰色的，好像要下雨。
column6: Tiānkōng shì huīsè de, hǎoxiàng yào xià yǔ.
column7: The sky is gray and it looks like rain.

column3: Purple, violet: 紫色, 紫外线 "ultraviolet", and the 紫禁城 "Forbidden City". As a color word, it can stand alone before a noun: 紫裙子, 紫葡萄. The silk radical 糸 shows a dyed thread, and 此 gives the sound (cǐ, zǐ). Purple was a color of rank in old China.
column6: Tā mǎi le yī tiáo zǐ qúnzi.
column7: She bought a purple skirt.

column3: An old color word for "green, blue, black" depending on the thing: 青草 "green grass", 青天 "blue sky", 青菜 "green vegetables", 青丝 "black hair". It also means "young": 青年 "young person", 青春 "youth". In the sense of color, it often describes fresh plants: 草青了 "the grass has turned green". Used in compounds more than alone.
column6: Chūntiān, shān shàng de cǎo qīng le.
column7: In spring the grass on the mountain turns green.

column3: Bright: 明亮的眼睛 "bright eyes", 灯光明亮 "brightly lit", 窗明几亮. It describes light, rooms, eyes, and colors. 明 puts the sun 日 and moon 月 together, as in the light of day; 亮 is a lit oil lamp, "bright" or "to shine". Also 亮 alone as a verb: 天亮了 "it has become light".
column6: Jiàoshì lǐ hěn míngliàng.
column7: The classroom is bright.

column3: Brightly colored, vivid: 色彩鲜艳 "vivid colors", 鲜艳的花 "bright flowers", 鲜艳夺目. It is for colors that catch the eye, often of flowers, clothes and fruit. 鲜 has fish 鱼 and sheep 羊, two fresh foods, and means "fresh"; 艳 comes from "rich" 丰 and "color" 色, "richly colored". The traditional 艷 can also be written 豔.
column4: 公园里开满了鲜艳的花。
column5: 公園裡開滿了鮮艷的花。
column6: Gōngyuán lǐ kāi mǎn le xiānyàn de huā.
column7: The park is full of brightly colored flowers.

column3: Community, neighborhood: 社区服务 "community service", 社区医院, 我们社区. It usually means the residential area managed by a neighborhood committee, a unit of city life in China. 社 is the "earth spirit" (the old altar of the land) and 区 "area". In Taiwan the usual word is 社區 as well, but 小区 is a mainland word for a housing complex.
column4: 我们社区有一个小图书馆。
column5: 我們社區有一個小圖書館。
column6: Wǒmen shèqū yǒu yī gè xiǎo túshūguǎn.
column7: Our neighborhood has a small library.

column3: Wharf, dock, pier: 货运码头 "freight dock", 在码头上等船, 港口码头. The 头 is neutral in speech. 码 is a stone 石 with 马 for the sound, and elsewhere means "number, code" (号码, 密码). 码头 also means "a trade hub".
column6: Chuán tíng zài mǎtou biān.
column7: The boat is moored at the dock.

column3: Hotel, guesthouse: 住宾馆 "stay at a hotel", 宾馆服务员. In mainland usage it often suggests a middle-range or state-run hotel, while a 酒店 is usually more upscale, 旅馆 is a small inn, and 饭店 means a hotel only in some names, such as 北京饭店. 宾 is "guest" and 馆 "building", so a "guest house". The upper part of 宾 is a roof 宀, with 兵 below in the simplified form.
column4: 我们住在车站附近的宾馆。
column5: 我們住在車站附近的賓館。
column6: Wǒmen zhù zài chēzhàn fùjìn de bīnguǎn.
column7: We are staying at a hotel near the station.

column3: Museum: 参观博物馆 "visit a museum", 历史博物馆, 故宫博物院 (the Palace Museum, which uses 院). 博 means "wide, rich" (as in 博士 "doctor") and 物 "things": 博物 is "a wide range of things", then 馆 "hall". Measure word 家 or 座: 一座博物馆.
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù le bówùguǎn.
column7: At the weekend we went to the museum.

column3: Reading room of a library or a school: 图书馆的阅览室, 报刊阅览室 "newspaper reading room". 阅 is "to read" (the door radical 门 and 兑) and 览 "to look at, to view"; 室 is "room". It is a quiet place for reading on the spot, not for borrowing. 阅读 "reading" is a more general word.
column6: Yuèlǎnshì lǐ hěn ānjìng.
column7: The reading room is very quiet.

column3: Club, a loanword (sound and meaning of 'club' mixed): 足球俱乐部 "football club", 健身俱乐部 "gym", 加入俱乐部 "join a club". The characters are chosen for meaning: 俱 "together" + 乐 "enjoy" + 部 "department, group". Here 乐 is read lè, "happy", not yuè "music".
column4: 他加入了一个足球俱乐部。
column5: 他加入了一個足球俱樂部。
column6: Tā jiārù le yī gè zúqiú jùlèbù.
column7: He joined a football club.

column3: Alley, lane, with the Beijing erhua ending: 胡同 is the narrow alley of an old Beijing quarter, and 胡同儿 is how Beijingers say it. 胡同 is read hútòng, with 同 in the fourth tone; the word comes from Mongolian and the characters are borrowed for sound. 逛胡同 "stroll through the hutongs" is a Beijing tourist outing.
column4: 老北京的胡同儿很有特色。
column5: 老北京的胡同兒很有特色。
column6: Lǎo Běijīng de hútòngr hěn yǒu tèsè.
column7: The hutongs of old Beijing have a special character.

column3: In the city, in town, as opposed to the countryside: 进城里 "go into town", 城里人 "city people", 住在城里. 城里 is a place word that does not need another 里. 城 has the earth radical 土 with 成 as the sound, because old city walls were rammed earth. 城 is "city wall" and "city".
column4: 他每天从郊区到城里上班。
column5: 他每天從郊區到城裡上班。
column6: Tā měitiān cóng jiāoqū dào chénglǐ shàngbān.
column7: Every day he goes from the suburbs into the city to work.

column3: Research institute on the mainland, and in Taiwan, "graduate school": 考研究所 "take the entrance exam for graduate school", 研究所毕业. In the mainland sense it is an institute, such as 语言研究所. 研 "to grind" and 究 "to look into" make 研究 "to research"; 所 is "place, institute".
column6: Tā xiǎng kǎo yánjiūsuǒ.
column7: He wants to take the graduate school entrance exam.

column3: Base: military, research, production or training: 军事基地, 生产基地 "production base", 培训基地 "training center". The word usually has a modifier in front. 基 is a "foundation", an earth radical 土 under 其, and 地 "ground". Often used in news about industry and science.
column4: 这个城市有一个大型科研基地。
column5: 這個城市有一個大型科研基地。
column6: Zhège chéngshì yǒu yī gè dàxíng kēyán jīdì.
column7: This city has a large scientific research base.

column3: Swimming pool: 室内游泳池 "indoor pool", 去游泳池游泳 "swim at the pool". 游泳 "swim" is made of two water-radical characters 游 and 泳, and 池 is "pond, pool". 游 also means "to roam" (游玩), and 泳 only occurs in "swim" words. Measure word 个.
column6: Jiǔdiàn lǐ yǒu yī gè yóuyǒngchí.
column7: The hotel has a swimming pool.

column3: Suburb, outskirts: 住在郊区 "live in the suburbs", 市区和郊区 "the city and its surroundings". 郊 has the place radical 阝 on the right and 交 on the left, which is the sound part and is the same sound (jiāo). Typically 市中心 is the city center, 郊区 the area around it.
column6: Tā zhù zài chéngshì de jiāoqū.
column7: He lives in the suburbs of the city.

column3: Countryside, home village, "township" (the administrative unit below a county): 家乡 "hometown", 乡下 "the countryside", 乡镇 "towns and townships", 同乡 "person from the same place". Seldom alone. Traditional 鄉 is quite different from the simplified 乡, in which a large part was dropped.
column6: Tā cóng xiāngxia láidào chéngshì.
column7: He came from the countryside to the city.

column3: Village, countryside: 乡村生活 "country life", 乡村旅游 "rural tourism", 乡村医生. It is a neutral and slightly written word that contrasts with 城市. 村 has 木 "tree" and 寸 for sound, and means "village". Compare 农村, the "farming village".
column6: Xiāngcūn de kōngqì bǐ chéngshì hǎo.
column7: The air in the countryside is better than in the city.

column3: Gardens, landscape garden: 苏州园林 "the gardens of Suzhou", the classic Chinese garden with rocks, ponds and pavilions; 园林设计 "garden design", 园林绿化 "landscaping". 园 is an "enclosure" 囗 with 元 inside; 林 is two trees, "grove" and "woods". The two words together give a park-like space.
column6: Sūzhōu de yuánlín hěn yǒumíng.
column7: The gardens of Suzhou are famous.

column3: Exposition, trade fair: 世界博览会 "World Expo", 国际博览会 "international fair", 汽车博览会 "auto show". The short form is 博览会 or 世博会. 博览 is "to see widely" (博 "broad", 览 "to look at") and 会 is "meeting". The pattern 举办博览会 "hold an expo" is typical.
column4: 这个城市举办过国际博览会。
column5: 這個城市舉辦過國際博覽會。
column6: Zhège chéngshì jǔbàn guo guójì bólǎnhuì.
column7: This city has held an international exposition.

column3: Warehouse, storehouse and "library, database": 仓库 "warehouse", 车库 "garage", 水库 "reservoir", 数据库 "database", 入库 "put into storage". It is a bound character, found nearly always in compounds. 库 is a building 广 with a cart 车 inside, the old way of showing a place to store carriages.
column6: Huòwù dōu fàng zài cāngkù lǐ.
column7: The goods are all kept in the warehouse.

column3: To ride, to travel by, and "to take advantage of": 乘飞机 "go by plane", 乘船, 乘车, 乘机 "seize the chance", 乘风破浪 "ride the wind and cleave the waves". In math it is "to multiply": 三乘四. 乘 is a written, more formal choice than 坐 and takes a vehicle as its object. The old picture is a person climbing a tree, shown with the feet.
column6: Wǒmen chéng fēijī qù Shànghǎi.
column7: We are going to Shanghai by plane.

column3: To ride in a vehicle: 乘车 is a verb-object word meaning to travel by bus, train or car: 乘车须知 "rules for riding", 乘车码 "ride code", 买票乘车. It sounds more official than 坐车 and appears on signs and in announcements. 车 is a simplified cart seen from above; the cart wheels have been written as strokes.
column6: Xiǎohái chéngchē yào jì ānquándài.
column7: Children must wear a seat belt when riding in a car.

column3: Passenger of a bus, train, plane or ship: 乘客朋友们 is used in announcements, 全体乘客 "all passengers". 乘 "to ride" + 客 "guest": a traveler is treated as a guest of the carrier. 旅客 is a "traveler", while 乘客 is someone riding a particular vehicle at this time.
column6: Měi wèi chéngkè dōu yǒu zuòwèi.
column7: Every passenger has a seat.

column3: To ride, to travel by, formal, with a vehicle as object: 乘坐飞机, 乘坐地铁, 乘坐本次航班 "take this flight". It sounds like a notice or an announcement; in conversation 坐 alone is more natural. 坐 shows two people 从 on the ground 土, "to sit". Do not use it for sitting on a chair.
column6: Huānyíng chéngzuò běn cì hángbān.
column7: Welcome aboard this flight.

column3: To drive, to pilot a vehicle, ship or aircraft, and "the driver": 驾驶汽车, 驾驶飞机, 驾驶员 "driver, pilot", 驾驶证 "driving license". It is more formal than 开车. Both characters carry the horse radical 马, left over from horse-drawn travel; 驶 has 史 as the sound, and 驾 has 加.
column6: Tā jiàshǐ zhe yī liàng xīn chē.
column7: He is driving a new car.

column3: Driver's license, short for 驾驶执照: 考驾照 "take a driving test", 拿驾照 "get a license", 驾照到期 "the license has expired". It is the spoken short form of the official 驾驶证. 照 here is "license, permit", as in 执照 and 护照 "passport", and also "photo" in 照片. Its fire radical 灬 goes with "bright".
column6: Tā gāng kǎodào jiàzhào.
column7: He has just got his driver's license.

column3: To travel, to run along a road or route, said of vehicles: 列车行驶 "the train runs", 限速行驶 "drive at a limited speed", 安全行驶 "drive safely". The subject is a vehicle, not a person; people use 走 or 开. 行 is read xíng, from a crossroads picture; 驶 is "to go fast", with the horse radical.
column6: Huǒchē zhèngzài píngwěn de xíngshǐ.
column7: The train is running smoothly.

column3: Motorbike, a loanword from "motor", short for 摩托车: 骑摩托 "ride a motorbike", 摩托头盔. Only the first two syllables of 摩托车 are used when speaking casually. In Taiwan a scooter is 机车, an ordinary motorcycle 摩托车, and a big, powerful one 重机 (重型机车). 托 has the hand 扌 and 乇 as sound (tuō), "to support".
column6: Tā qí mótuō shàngbān.
column7: He rides a motorbike to work.

column3: Vehicle owner: 车主请注意 "owners, please note", 车主信息. 主 is "owner, master" and in its form a lamp with a flame, which became the "master of the house". It is also in 房主 "owner of a house" and 店主 "shop owner". A word from parking signs and from forms.
column6: Chēzhǔ qǐng bǎ chē kāi zǒu.
column7: Car owners, please move your cars.

column3: Guide who leads the way, on a trip or in the mountains: 做向导, 当地向导 "local guide", 请向导. A person who shows the way, as opposed to 导游, a "tour guide" who also explains. 向 is "direction, toward" and 导 "to lead", with a hand 寸 pointing. The traditional 嚮導 uses a form of 向 that is rarely seen in the simplified.
column4: 我们请了一位当地人做向导。
column5: 我們請了一位當地人做嚮導。
column6: Wǒmen qǐng le yī wèi dāngdìrén zuò xiàngdǎo.
column7: We hired a local person as our guide.

column3: To return, to go back to a place: 返回北京 "return to Beijing", 返回原处, 返回首页 "go back to the home page". Somewhat formal; the object is the place one goes back to. 返 is "to turn back" (the walking radical 辶 and 反 "reverse") and 回 "return" is a spiral. 回来 and 回去 are the spoken words.
column6: Tāmen míngtiān jiù fǎnhuí Běijīng.
column7: They return to Beijing tomorrow.

column3: The whole way, all along the journey: 一路上 "on the way", 一路顺风 and 一路平安 "have a good trip", 一路走好. It can also mean "of the same kind": 一路人, 一路货. 一路 comes before the verb: 一路跑回家 "ran all the way home". Farewells use 祝你一路平安 as a set wish. 路 has 足 "foot" and 各.
column6: Zhù nǐ yīlù píng'ān!
column7: Have a safe trip!

column3: Deposit that is paid and returned later: 交押金 "pay a deposit", 退押金 "refund the deposit", 押金条 "deposit receipt". Common with rented bikes, rooms and hotels. 押 means "to pledge, to hold" and has the hand 扌 with 甲, which is the sound (jiǎ, yā); 金 is "money, gold", picturing a bell of metal.
column4: 租自行车要交一百块押金。
column5: 租自行車要交一百塊押金。
column6: Zū zìxíngchē yào jiāo yībǎi kuài yājīn.
column7: You have to pay a deposit of one hundred yuan to rent a bike.

column3: To pack up, and above all "to take leftovers home from a restaurant": 服务员，打包 "please pack this up", 打包带走 "pack to take away". It also means "to bundle" things for shipment or files in a computer: 打包文件. 打 is used in many verbs and 包 is a swaddled baby, "wrap". Take-out food is also 外卖 or 带走.
column4: 菜太多了，请帮我们打包。
column5: 菜太多了，請幫我們打包。
column6: Cài tài duō le, qǐng bāng wǒmen dǎbāo.
column7: There is too much food. Please pack the rest for us.

column3: To go on a business trip: 去上海出差 "go to Shanghai on business", 出差回来, 出差补助. A verb-object word, so you can say 出了一趟差 "went on one trip". 差 is read chāi here ("errand, mission"), not chà "to lack" or chā "difference". The person is working away; a holiday trip is 旅行.
column6: Tā xià zhōu yào qù Shànghǎi chūchāi.
column7: He is going on a business trip to Shanghai next week.
