column3: To move, to transport: 运货 "transport goods", 运到北京 "ship to Beijing", and "fortune, luck": 运气, 好运, 命运 "fate". It also builds 运动 "sports, movement". In the sense of moving things, it usually has a place after it: 运到…. 运 has the walking radical 辶 and 云 as the sound (yún, yùn).
column6: Zhèxiē shuǐguǒ yào yùn dào Běijīng.
column7: These fruits are going to be shipped to Beijing.

column3: Volume, booklet and the measure word for books of a set: 一册书, 第二册 "volume two", 手册 "handbook", 相册 "photo album". In the old script the character pictures bamboo strips tied together, the first form of a book. The measure word 本 is more usual for a book; 册 is for volumes of one work.
column6: Zhè tào shū yīgòng yǒu sān cè.
column7: This set of books has three volumes in all.

column3: Measure word for flowers, clouds, and things that look like them: 一朵花 "a flower", 一朵云 "a cloud", 两朵玫瑰. As a noun it is the ear's lobe in 耳朵 "ear", where 朵 is neutral. The shape is 几 over 木: flowers drooping from a tree. Do not use it for whole plants (棵) or bunches (束).
column6: Tiānshàng yǒu jǐ duǒ báiyún.
column7: There are a few white clouds in the sky.

column3: Measure word for small round things: 一颗星星 "a star", 一颗糖 "a candy", 一颗心 "a heart", 一颗牙, 一颗珍珠 "a pearl", also satellites. It stands before the noun like 个 but only for small, grain-like objects. The word 页 on the right is the "head" radical, referring to something round like a head.
column6: Tā chī le yī kē táng.
column7: She ate a candy.

column3: Measure word for horses, mules and bolts of cloth: 一匹马, 两匹骡子, 一匹布. Alone it appears in 匹配 "to match", with 匹 as "a match, a counterpart". The character is a roll of cloth in old forms. For other animals use 只 or 头. The typical form is the number + 匹 + 马.
column6: Cǎoyuán shàng yǒu jǐ pǐ mǎ.
column7: There are a few horses on the grassland.

column3: Measure word for pictures and cloth: 一幅画 "a painting", 一幅照片, 一幅地图 "a map", 一幅对联. As a noun it means "width", as in 篇幅 "length of an article" and 幅度 "range, extent". 幅 has the cloth radical 巾 with 畐 as the sound. A flat hanging object, not a three-dimensional one.
column6: Qiáng shàng guà zhe yī fú shānshuǐ huà.
column7: A landscape painting hangs on the wall.

column3: A pile, a heap and also the measure word: 一堆书, 一堆人 "a crowd", 一堆问题 "a pile of problems". As a verb it means "to pile up": 堆在一起. It is not exact: 一堆 gives the sense of "lots, a heap". 堆 has the earth radical 土 on the left, and 隹 on the right as the sound part; earth was the first thing to be heaped up.
column6: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yī duī shū.
column7: There is a pile of books on the table.

column3: Session, a term of office and the measure word for events held in series: 第一届 "the first session", 本届 "this year's", 应届毕业生 "this year's graduates", 历届 "all previous". It is placed after 第 and a number: 第三十二届奥运会. 届 also means "to arrive (at a time)", as in 届时 "at that time".
column4: 这是第三十二届奥运会。
column5: 這是第三十二屆奧運會。
column6: Zhè shì dì sānshí'èr jiè Àoyùnhuì.
column7: This is the thirty-second Olympic Games.

column3: Size, height, build of a person or thing: 个儿高 "tall", 大个儿, 高个儿 "a tall person", 挑个儿大的 "pick the big ones". An erhua word of the north, spoken only. Read gèr.
column4: 他个儿很高，打篮球很合适。
column5: 他個兒很高，打籃球很合適。
column6: Tā gèr hěn gāo, dǎ lánqiú hěn héshì.
column7: He is tall and well suited to basketball.

column3: The whole body, "from head to foot", and "a suit of clothes": 一身汗 "covered in sweat", 一身新衣服 "a new set of clothes", 一身泥 "covered in mud", 一身轻松 "relaxed". It is mostly followed by a noun for what covers the body, and is placed after a verb of 出 or 穿: 出了一身汗, 穿一身黑. 身 is a pregnant woman in the oldest form.
column6: Tā chū le yīshēn hàn.
column7: He broke out in a sweat all over.

column3: In one breath, at a stretch: 一口气跑到山顶, 一口气喝完, 一口气说完. It goes before the verb for something done in one go without stopping. Also 松了一口气 "breathed a sigh of relief", where 一口气 is the object. 口 is an open mouth, and 气 "breath, air" shows rising vapor.
column6: Tā yīkǒuqì pǎo dào le shāndǐng.
column7: He ran to the top of the hill without stopping.

column3: Suddenly, all at once, in no time: 一下子就明白了 "understood at once", 一下子全忘了 "forgot everything at a stroke". It goes before the verb and means the action is quick or unexpected, a bit more colloquial than 突然. The 一下 after a verb is different, meaning "for a moment": 看一下.
column6: Tā yīxiàzi zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: He stood up all of a sudden.

column3: In a word, in short, used before a decision or a demand: 一句话，你去不去？ "tell me straight, are you going?" 一句话，我同意 "in a word, I agree". It can also mean literally "one sentence". Used on its own to bring a talk to a conclusion. 句 is a measure word for sentences, and 话 "speech" has the speech radical 讠.
column6: Yījùhuà, nǐ dàodǐ qù bu qù?
column7: In a word, are you going or not?

column3: Ton, a loanword for the unit of weight (1,000 kg): 一吨货, 三吨水, 吨位 "tonnage". The mouth radical 口 marks it as a borrowed sound and 屯 gives a rough sound (tún, dūn). A ton is also 公吨 in weights and measures.
column6: Zhè liàng kǎchē néng zhuāng wǔ dūn huò.
column7: This truck can carry five tons of goods.

column3: A traditional unit of length, about 3.3 cm (a "Chinese inch"), and "very small": 一寸 "an inch", 寸步难行 "unable to take a step", 尺寸 "size". 英寸 is the English inch. The picture is a hand with a dot marking the place where the pulse is felt, about an inch up the wrist. Photos are measured in 寸: 五寸照片.
column6: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn shì wǔ cùn de.
column7: This photo is five inches.

column3: Second, the unit of time: 十秒, 一秒钟, 秒表 "stopwatch", and "arc second". On the net 秒 is also a verb or adverb: 秒杀 "to sell out in seconds, to crush instantly", 秒回 "reply at once". The grain radical 禾 refers to the awn at the tip of grain, a tiny thing, and 少 gives the sound.
column4: 他用十秒跑完了一百米。
column5: 他用十秒跑完了一百米。
column6: Tā yòng shí miǎo pǎo wán le yībǎi mǐ.
column7: He ran one hundred meters in ten seconds.

column3: New Year's Day, 1 January, a public holiday: 元旦快乐 "happy New Year", 过元旦. Not the Lunar New Year, which is 春节. 元 is "first" (a figure with the head marked) and 旦 is the sun 日 rising over the horizon 一, "dawn". So 元旦 is "the first morning" of the year. A three-day 元旦 holiday is common.
column4: 元旦那天，我们一起吃饭。
column5: 元旦那天，我們一起吃飯。
column6: Yuándàn nà tiān, wǒmen yīqǐ chīfàn.
column7: On New Year's Day we eat together.

column3: New Year's Eve of the lunar calendar, the night before the Spring Festival, when the whole family eats the reunion dinner (年夜饭) and stays up late: 除夕夜, 守岁 "stay up the night". 除 means "to remove, to clear away" the old year and 夕 is "evening", a crescent moon. The 除 appears in 除了 "except" and 除法 "division".
column4: 除夕晚上全家人一起吃年夜饭。
column5: 除夕晚上全家人一起吃年夜飯。
column6: Chúxī wǎnshang quánjiārén yīqǐ chī niányèfàn.
column7: On New Year's Eve the whole family eats the reunion dinner together.

column3: The Mid-Autumn Festival, on the 15th day of the eighth lunar month, when the moon is fullest and families get together to eat mooncakes (月饼): 过中秋节, 中秋节快乐. 秋 is "autumn", made of grain 禾 and fire 火, the harvest season; 节 is "festival", the sections of bamboo, hence "joint". It is often shortened to 中秋.
column4: 中秋节是家人团聚的日子。
column5: 中秋節是家人團聚的日子。
column6: Zhōngqiūjié shì jiārén tuánjù de rìzi.
column7: The Mid-Autumn Festival is a day for families to get together.

column3: Week and "Sunday" in speech, in southern China and in Taiwan, where 星期 is just as usual: 下个礼拜 "next week", 礼拜一 "Monday", 礼拜天 "Sunday". The mainland also writes 周. Its first meaning is "religious service", 做礼拜 "attend worship". 拜 is two hands 手 together in respect: "to bow, to pay respects".
column6: Xià ge lǐbài wǒmen qù lǚxíng.
column7: Next week we are going on a trip.

column3: Workday, weekday as opposed to 周末 or 节假日: 工作日 加班 "work overtime on a weekday", 工作日不送货 "no delivery on weekdays", 三个工作日内 "within three working days". It is used in rules and notices more than in chat. 工 is a tool and 日 the sun, "day"; 作 "to do" is a person 亻 and 乍.
column4: 工作日我早上七点起床。
column5: 工作日我早上七點起床。
column6: Gōngzuòrì wǒ zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
column7: On weekdays I get up at seven.

column3: Today, the written word: 今日新闻 "today's news", 今日头条 "today's headlines", 今日有雨 "rain today". In speech it is 今天; 今日 belongs to signs, headlines, announcements and set phrases. 今 is "now" and 日 "day". Its older sense is the same as English "this day".
column6: Jīnrì yǒu yǔ, qǐng dài sǎn.
column7: There will be rain today, please bring an umbrella.

column3: Early morning, the first hours after dawn: 清晨的空气 "the air in the early morning", 在清晨出发. A written, pleasant word. 清 is "clear, fresh" with water 氵 and the sound 青; 晨 is "morning" (日 and 辰). 早上 is the everyday word, and 凌晨 means the small hours after midnight.
column6: Qīngchén de kōngqì tèbié xīnxiān.
column7: The air is especially fresh in the early morning.

column3: At night, during the night: 夜间行驶 "drive at night", 夜间门诊 "night clinic", 夜间部 "evening classes". It is a formal word for a time of day, used for rules, services and schedules. The opposite is 白天 or 日间. 间 is "between" and shows a door 门 with the sun 日 in the gap.
column6: Yèjiān qǐng bùyào dàshēng shuōhuà.
column7: Please don't talk loudly at night.

column3: Year as a period of accounts or school, "annual": 年度总结 "annual review", 年度报告 "annual report", 年度最佳 "of the year", 财政年度 "fiscal year". 年 is "year" and 度 means a "span, degree". It describes a year as a unit of work or finance, not just any 365 days, so don't use it to count years.
column6: Gōngsī yào xiě niándù zǒngjié.
column7: The company has to write an annual review.

column3: Before the new year: the weeks before the Spring Festival, short for 过年前 in speech: 年前把工作做完 "finish the work before New Year", 年前年后 "before and after New Year". Note that in 三年前 "three years ago" the 年 belongs to the count 三年, so that is not this word. 前 shows a foot moving forward on a boat.
column4: 年前我们要把工作做完。
column5: 年前我們要把工作做完。
column6: Niánqián wǒmen yào bǎ gōngzuò zuò wán.
column7: Before the New Year we have to finish the work.

column3: In those years, back then: 当年他还是个学生 "back then he was a student", 想当年 "when I think of those days". The same characters, read dàngnián, mean "the same year" (当年完成 "completed within the year"). It also means "the prime of life": 当年的小伙子. 当 is read dāng here, meaning "at that time".
column6: Dāngnián tā hái shì ge xuésheng.
column7: Back then he was still a student.

column3: Cycle, period: 生长周期 "growth cycle", 周期性 "periodic", 一个周期 "one cycle", 周期表 "periodic table". It is the length of time at which something repeats: of a plant, the moon, an economy or a production run. 周 here means "round", as in 周围 "surroundings", and 期 "period" has the moon 月 and 其.
column4: 这种植物的生长周期很短。
column5: 這種植物的生長週期很短。
column6: Zhè zhǒng zhíwù de shēngzhǎng zhōuqī hěn duǎn.
column7: This plant has a very short growth cycle.

column3: Years, time as it passes, in a literary and emotional way: 岁月流逝 "years go by", 艰苦的岁月 "years of hardship", 岁月如梭 "time flies like a shuttle". It is used in writing and songs for a long stretch of life. 岁 means "year of age" and shows a mountain 山 over an evening 夕, in the simplified form; 月 "month".
column6: Suìyuè guò de zhēn kuài.
column7: Time passes so fast.

column3: Time, a period seen as something that passes, with feeling: 美好的时光 "a happy time", 时光飞逝 "time flies", 浪费时光 "waste time". It is a written word, close to 岁月 but for shorter, usually pleasant periods. 时 is the simplified 時 with 寸 for the sound part, and 光 here is "scene, moment".
column4: 我们度过了一段美好的时光。
column5: 我們度過了一段美好的時光。
column6: Wǒmen dùguò le yī duàn měihǎo de shíguāng.
column7: We spent a wonderful time together.

column3: To turn one's head and "later": 他回头看了一眼 "he looked back", and in speech 回头见 "see you later", 回头再说 "talk about it later", 回头给你打电话 "I'll call you later". The second use is vague about when and is typical of the north. It can also mean "repent": 浪子回头.
column4: 我现在有事，回头再给你打电话。
column5: 我現在有事，回頭再給你打電話。
column6: Wǒ xiànzài yǒu shì, huítóu zài gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
column7: I'm busy now, I'll call you later.

column3: Superstition, and "to be superstitious about, to have blind faith in": 封建迷信 "feudal superstition", 迷信风水, 迷信权威 "blindly trust authority". It is negative and applies to people who believe without evidence. 迷 is "lost, deluded" and 信 "belief". 信 is also "letter" and "trust": 相信.
column6: Tā bù xiāngxìn míxìn.
column7: He doesn't believe in superstition.

column3: God, spirit: 拜神 "worship a god", 神仙 "an immortal", 神话 "myth". It also means "mind, energy" (精神, 眼神 "the look in the eyes") and "magical, amazing": 太神了！ "that's incredible!". The left part 礻 is the spirit radical; the right 申 was originally a drawing of lightning, once a sign of the gods.
column4: 他们每年都去庙里拜神。
column5: 他們每年都去廟裡拜神。
column6: Tāmen měi nián dōu qù miào lǐ bài shén.
column7: Every year they go to the temple to worship the gods.

column3: Ghost and "devil": 见鬼 "damn it", 鬼故事 "ghost story", 鬼节 "Ghost Festival". It is also a suffix (酒鬼) and a word for "sly": 鬼点子 "a sly idea". In Chinese belief a 鬼 is the spirit of a dead person. The picture is a figure with a mask-like face. Used for children's fears, folk tales and swearing.
column6: Xiǎoháizi dōu pà guǐ.
column7: All children are afraid of ghosts.

column3: The present, at this time: 当前形势 "the present situation", 当前的任务 "the task at hand", 当前最重要的是… "what matters most now is…". A formal word of speeches and news. 当 means "to face" here (as in 当面) and 前 "front", so "right in front of us" in time. Used as a modifier or at the start of a clause.
column6: Dāngqián zuì zhòngyào de shì ānquán.
column7: What matters most at present is safety.

column3: The present age, contemporary: 当代文学, 当代艺术, 当代大学生. It points to the era we live in, whereas 现代 is "modern times" in a longer sense, since about 1919. 代 has a person 亻 and 弋 for the sound, and means "generation, era".
column6: Tā xǐhuan dāngdài yìshù.
column7: He likes contemporary art.

column3: This moment, right now: 此刻的心情 "the mood of this moment", 此时此刻 "at this very moment". Written, often at the start of a sentence. 此 is "this" (a foot 止 stopping by a person: "here") and 刻 "a moment, a quarter hour", which first means "to carve", and a knife 刂 is on its right.
column4: 此刻，我心里充满了感谢。
column5: 此刻，我心裡充滿了感謝。
column6: Cǐkè, wǒ xīnli chōngmǎn le gǎnxiè.
column7: At this moment I am full of gratitude.

column3: At this time, by now: 此时天已经黑了 "by then it was already dark", 此时此刻 "at this very moment". It looks at a time in the story or the situation under discussion, which can be past or present; 此刻 is closer to "now". Written style, placed in front of the main clause.
column6: Cǐshí tiān yǐjīng hēi le.
column7: By then it was already dark.

column3: Recently, lately: 近来天气变化很大 "the weather has changed a lot lately", 近来好吗？ "how have you been?". A bit more formal than 最近. It goes at the start of the sentence or before the verb and refers to the last few days or weeks up to now. 近 has the walking radical 辶 and 斤 "axe" as the sound.
column6: Jìnlái tiānqì biànhuà hěn dà.
column7: The weather has changed a lot lately.

column3: Currently existing, available: 现有的条件 "the existing conditions", 现有资源 "available resources", 利用现有设备. It is only used before a noun, with or without 的. 现 is "now, current" and 有 "to have", so "what is now at hand". 现 has the jade radical 王 and 见; the same 现 is in 现在, 出现 and 现状.
column4: 我们要充分利用现有的资源。
column5: 我們要充分利用現有的資源。
column6: Wǒmen yào chōngfèn lìyòng xiànyǒu de zīyuán.
column7: We should make full use of the resources we have.

column3: The present situation, the status quo: 了解现状 "understand the situation", 改变现状 "change the status quo", 现状不容乐观 "the situation is not optimistic". It is the standard word in reports, news and talk about problems. 状 means "shape, condition" (as in 状态 and 情状); the 犬 radical is a leftover from older forms.
column4: 他对自己的现状很不满意。
column5: 他對自己的現狀很不滿意。
column6: Tā duì zìjǐ de xiànzhuàng hěn bù mǎnyì.
column7: He is very dissatisfied with his present situation.

column3: Temporary, for the time being: 暂时的困难 "temporary trouble", 暂时不去 "won't go for now", 暂时停止. It works as an adjective before 的 and as an adverb before a verb. 暂 shows the sun 日 with 斩 "cut" (the traditional 暫 has 斬): a short stretch of time cut off. It does not say how long, just that it is not final.
column6: Zhè zhǐ shì zànshí de kùnnan.
column7: This is only a temporary difficulty.

column3: Before, earlier: 比先前瘦了 "thinner than before", 先前的计划 "the earlier plan", 先前提到过 "mentioned earlier". Written and a little formal, like 之前; it refers to a past time before another time in the story. 先 is a foot stepping in front of a person: "go first". 前 has the same sense of "before, in front" in time.
column6: Tā bǐ xiānqián shòu le hěn duō.
column7: He is much thinner than before.

column3: Originally, at first: 原先的计划 "the original plan", 原先以为… "I originally thought…". It contrasts the first state with a later change: 原先他住在乡下，现在搬到了城里. 原 shows a spring from a cliff, the source, hence "origin"; 先 is "first". It can be an adverb or a modifier with 的.
column6: Yuánxiān de jìhuà gǎibiàn le.
column7: The original plan has changed.

column3: Original, previously existing: 原有的设施 "the original facilities", 保持原有风格 "keep the original style". It is only used as a modifier before a noun and implies that something has since been added or changed. Compare 现有, which is "existing now"; 原有 is "what was there at the start". 原 is "original" and 有 "to have".
column4: 他们保留了房子原有的样子。
column5: 他們保留了房子原有的樣子。
column6: Tāmen bǎoliú le fángzi yuányǒu de yàngzi.
column7: They kept the house's original look.

column3: In the past, formerly: 与以往不同 "different from before", 比以往更… "more … than ever", 以往的经验 "past experience". It places the present against a long past, as a noun, a modifier or an adverb. 往 is "to go (toward)" with the step radical 彳; 以 is "by means of", here part of "up to".
column4: 今年的夏天比以往更热。
column5: 今年的夏天比以往更熱。
column6: Jīnnián de xiàtiān bǐ yǐwǎng gèng rè.
column7: This summer is hotter than ever.

column3: Early period, early stage: 早期作品 "early works", 早期教育 "early education", 早期发现 "early detection". It is often used for an earlier part of a longer span, such as someone's career or a historical age. 早 is "early", the sun 日 above a mark; 期 "period" has the moon 月 and 其 for the sound.
column6: Zhè shì tā zǎoqī de zuòpǐn.
column7: This is one of his early works.

column3: Initial stage, the beginning: 工作初期 "the early days of a job", 发展初期 "the beginning of development". It is a shorter stretch than 早期, the very first part. 初 shows a knife 刀 and the clothes radical 衤: cutting the cloth is the first step of making a garment, hence "first, beginning".
column4: 工作初期遇到了很多困难。
column5: 工作初期遇到了很多困難。
column6: Gōngzuò chūqī yùdào le hěn duō kùnnan.
column7: In the early days of the job there were many difficulties.

column3: Primitive, original, first-hand: 原始社会 "primitive society", 原始森林 "virgin forest", 原始数据 "raw data", 原始记录. It describes something in its first state, untouched, and sometimes "simple, undeveloped". 始 "beginning" has the woman radical 女 and 台 as the sound (tái, shǐ), a weak match; 原 is "source, origin".
column6: Zhèlǐ bǎoliú zhe yuánshǐ sēnlín.
column7: Virgin forest has been preserved here.

column3: After this, from then on: 此后再没回来过 "never came back after that", 此后的几年 "the years after". Written; the starting point is a past event just mentioned, unlike 以后, which is general. It begins a clause and the subject follows. In traditional writing this 后 is 後; 后 there is a different character, "queen".
column4: 他十八岁离开家，此后再没回去过。
column5: 他十八歲離開家，此後再沒回去過。
column6: Tā shíbā suì líkāi jiā, cǐhòu zài méi huí qù guo.
column7: He left home at eighteen and never went back after that.

column3: Soon after, afterwards: 你先走，我随后就到 "you go first, I'll come right after", 随后又说 "then added". It means "right after something" and is used with 就 or 又. 随 means "to follow" and in the simplified form has a place radical 阝 and a walking part. It is used for what follows closely in a story.
column6: Nǐ xiān zǒu, wǒ suíhòu jiù dào.
column7: You go first, I'll be there right behind you.

column3: Successively, one after another and "order of before and after": 他们先后到达了北京 "they arrived one after the other", 先后顺序 "sequence", 不分先后 "in no particular order". It shows several events in a row or a ranking. 先 is "first" and 后 "after". The word before the verb is an adverb.
column6: Tāmen xiānhòu dàodá le Běijīng.
column7: They arrived in Beijing one after another.

column3: On the spot, at the scene: 当场抓住 "catch red-handed", 当场死亡 "die at the scene", 当场表示 "state on the spot". It stands before the verb to say the action happened right where the event was, with no delay. 当 is read dāng and 场 chǎng, "place". 场 has the earth radical 土 on its left.
column4: 小偷被警察当场抓住了。
column5: 小偷被警察當場抓住了。
column6: Xiǎotōu bèi jǐngchá dāngchǎng zhuāzhù le.
column7: The thief was caught on the spot by the police.

column3: To pull something out of where it is fixed: 拔草 "pull weeds", 拔牙 "have a tooth pulled", 拔河 "tug of war". It also means to stand out or to raise, as in 海拔 "height above sea level". The right half 犮 is only a sound part and says little today; the hand 扌 on the left is the clue that this is done with the hands.
column6: Tā bá le yī gēn cǎo.
column7: He pulled out a blade of grass.

column3: To stick something into something else: 插花 "arrange flowers", 插头 "plug", 插座 "socket", 插嘴 "interrupt a speaker". The pattern is 把 + thing + 插 + 在/进 + place. It also means to take part in something, as in 插手, usually where you were not asked.
column6: Tā bǎ huā chā zài huāpíng lǐ.
column7: He put the flowers in the vase.

column3: To take apart something that was put together or closed: 拆房子 "tear down a house", 拆信 "open a letter", 拆包裹 "unpack a parcel". Often followed by a result word, as in 拆开 and 拆掉. Its opposite is 装 or 建. In Chinese cities 拆 also became a well-known word for demolishing old housing.
column6: Tāmen yào chāi zhè zuò jiù lóu.
column7: They are going to tear down this old building.

column3: To lift or carry something with the hands or a team: 抬东西 "lift things", 两个人抬桌子 "two people carry a table". It also means to raise a part of the body: 抬手, 抬头 "raise one's head", 抬腿. Unlike 拿, the thing is heavy or is carried by several people. 扌 is the hand and 台 the sound.
column4: 我们一起把桌子抬上楼。
column5: 我們一起把桌子抬上樓。
column6: Wǒmen yīqǐ bǎ zhuōzi tái shàng lóu.
column7: Let's carry the table upstairs together.

column3: To steady or help someone with your hand: 扶老人过马路 "help an old person cross the road", 扶着栏杆 "hold on to the rail", and 扶起 "help up". Also used for supporting a cause, as in 扶贫 "help the poor out of poverty". The sound part 夫 is the same as in 丈夫 and 夫妻.
column6: Tā fú zhe lǎorén guò mǎlù.
column7: He helped the old man across the road.

column3: To throw, in the sense of throwing away or tossing: 扔垃圾 "throw out rubbish", 把球扔给我 "toss me the ball". Spoken and very common, and it is also what you do to something you do not want. For throwing in sport or aiming, 投 is used. The 乃 on the right only hints at the sound.
column6: Bié bǎ lājī rēng zài dìshang.
column7: Don't throw rubbish on the ground.

column3: To hand something over or pass it along: 递东西 "pass something", 递纸条 "pass a note", 传递 "convey", 快递 "express delivery". Usually used with a direction word: 递过来 "hand it over to me", 递过去 "hand it to them". The traditional 遞 keeps 辶 "walk" on the left, which fits the idea of something moving along.
column6: Qǐng bǎ nà běn shū dì guòlái.
column7: Please hand me that book.

column3: To hand something to someone: 递给 + person, or 把 + thing + 递给 + person. 给 marks the receiver, so the person always follows. In speech you can say just 给 or 递 when the direction is clear, but 递给 is exact when you pass something across a table or from one person to another.
column6: Tā bǎ bēizi dìgěi le wǒ.
column7: He handed the cup to me.

column3: To hold something between two things, such as chopsticks, tongs, or the arm and body: 用筷子夹菜 "pick up food with chopsticks", 夹在中间 "stuck in the middle". As a noun it is a clip or folder, usually with 子: 夹子, 文件夹. The shape of 夹 is a person 大 with a small stroke on each side, which is the idea of being squeezed between two things.
column6: Tā yòng kuàizi jiā le yī kuài ròu.
column7: He picked up a piece of meat with chopsticks.

column3: To pick or take off something that is attached: 摘苹果 "pick apples", 摘花 "pick flowers", 摘眼镜 "take off one's glasses", 摘帽子 "take off a hat". With clothes it works for items worn on the head or face; for most clothes use 脱 instead. 摘 can also mean to extract, as in 摘要 "summary".
column4: 她在树上摘了一个苹果。
column5: 她在樹上摘了一個蘋果。
column6: Tā zài shù shang zhāi le yī ge píngguǒ.
column7: She picked an apple from the tree.

column3: To stretch out a limb or something long: 伸手 "reach out a hand", 伸出舌头 "stick out the tongue", 伸懒腰 "stretch", 伸直 "straighten". Often followed by 出 or 进. The sound part 申 is the same in 神 and 绅, both read shēn. 亻 is a person, so it is a person stretching.
column6: Qǐng bǎ shǒu shēn chūlái.
column7: Please stretch your hand out.

column3: To hold in the hand and keep a grip: 握手 "shake hands", 握紧 "grip tightly", 握拳 "clench a fist". It also means to hold in the sense of control, as in 掌握 "to master". The sound part 屋 is the same character as "house", which no longer sounds quite alike. 扌 on the left is the hand.
column6: Tā jǐnjǐn wò zhe wǒ de shǒu.
column7: He held my hand tightly.

column3: To knock or tap on something with a short, repeated blow: 敲门 "knock on a door", 敲桌子 "tap the table", 敲鼓 "beat a drum", 敲键盘 "type on a keyboard". In spoken Chinese 敲 can also mean to overcharge someone, as in 敲竹杠. The right side 攴 is a hand with a stick, the sign of striking.
column6: Tā yòng shǒuzhǐ qiāo zhe zhuōzi.
column7: He was tapping the table with his finger.

column3: To knock on a door: 敲门声 "the sound of knocking", 有人敲门 "someone is knocking". Because the object 门 is built in, you do not add another object. Use 敲 on its own for other things, such as 敲窗户. Chinese people often knock in several taps in a row, 敲了三下 "knocked three times".
column6: Yǒu rén zài qiāomén.
column7: Someone is knocking at the door.

column3: To shake the head, meaning "no", disapproval or helplessness: 摇摇头 "shake one's head", 连连摇头 "keep shaking one's head". The partner is 点头 "nod". Both are separable verbs, so the verb can be doubled in the middle: 摇了摇头. 摇 is "to shake" and 头 "head".
column6: Tā tīng le zhǐshì yáotóu.
column7: When he heard it, he just shook his head.

column3: To wave a hand to greet someone, call them over, or stop a vehicle: 向他招手 "wave to him", 招手叫出租车 "wave down a taxi". It is a separable verb, so aspect marks and objects go in the middle, as in 招了招手. 招 is also "to beckon" and "to recruit", as in 招聘.
column6: Tā xiàng wǒ zhāoshǒu.
column7: She waved to me.

column3: To clap, to applaud: 热烈鼓掌 "applaud warmly", 为他鼓掌 "applaud him", 鼓掌欢迎 "welcome with applause". It is a separable verb, so you can put 了 in the middle: 鼓了掌. 鼓 is "to beat" (as on a drum) and 掌 is the palm of the hand: you beat your palms together.
column6: Dàjiā dōu wèi tā gǔzhǎng.
column7: Everyone applauded him.

column3: To raise one's head and look up: 抬头看 "look up", 抬起头来 "lift one's head". Used for looking up at something or for facing someone without shame. Its opposite is 低头 "lower one's head". The word also has a figurative meaning, "to rise or recover", which you may meet in news about prices or markets.
column6: Tā táitóu kàn le kàn tiān.
column7: He looked up at the sky.

column3: To hug, to embrace: 拥抱一下 "give a hug", 热情的拥抱 "a warm embrace". Both characters mean the same thing, to put your arms around someone, and both have the hand 扌. 拥 also means to crowd around, as in 拥挤 "crowded", and 拥有 "possess".
column4: 他们热情地拥抱在一起。
column5: 他們熱情地擁抱在一起。
column6: Tāmen rèqíng de yōngbào zài yīqǐ.
column7: They hugged each other warmly.

column3: To stand upright, and to set something up: 立着 "standing", 立刻 "at once", 立足 "have a footing", 成立 "to found". On its own it is somewhat written; in speech people say 站 for "stand". 立 is a person with arms wide (大) on top of a line, the ground, so it is a man standing on the ground.
column6: Yī kē dà shù lì zài lùbiān.
column7: A big tree stands by the road.

column3: To pick up something from the ground: 拾起 "pick up", 拾到钱包 "find a wallet", 拾金不昧 "not keep found money". It is more formal and written than 捡. The same character is a banker's form of the number ten, used on checks, so that it cannot be altered. 扌 is the hand and 合 the sound.
column6: Tā wān yāo bǎ shū shí le qǐlái.
column7: He bent down and picked up the book.

column3: To squeeze or press in, and to be crowded: 挤公交 "squeeze onto a bus", 别挤 "don't push", 挤出时间 "squeeze out some time", 挤牙膏 "squeeze toothpaste". As an adjective it means crowded: 很挤. Related word: 拥挤 "crowded". The traditional 擠 shows the sound part 齊 in full.
column6: Zǎoshang de dìtiě hěn jǐ.
column7: The subway is very crowded in the morning.

column3: To block or keep out: 挡路 "stand in the way", 挡雨 "keep off the rain", 挡风 "keep off the wind", 挡住视线 "block the view". The thing blocked usually follows, and 住 often follows 挡. The same character is the gear of a car, 挂挡 "shift gear", pronounced dǎng too. Simplified 挡 has 当 where 擋 has 當.
column6: Bié dǎng zhe wǒ de lù.
column7: Don't stand in my way.

column3: To play a plucked or keyed instrument: 弹钢琴 "play the piano", 弹吉他 "play the guitar", 弹琴. Also to flick or spring: 弹一下 "flick it", 弹跳 "bounce". When it means a bullet or bomb it is read dàn: 子弹, 炸弹. 弓 "bow" is the meaning part, which fits a plucked string.
column6: Tā huì tán gāngqín.
column7: She can play the piano.

column3: To fall and hit the ground, or to throw something down hard so that it may break: 摔了一跤 "had a fall", 摔跤 "wrestle", 摔坏 "drop and break", 把手机摔了. A person falls with 摔倒; you can also 摔 someone or something on purpose. You often see 摔 + a result word (摔伤, 摔碎). The hand 扌 shows that the action is a throw as well as a tumble.
column6: Tā bù xiǎoxīn shuāi le yī jiāo.
column7: He accidentally took a fall.

column3: To fall down, to lose one's footing: 摔倒在地 "fall to the ground", 小心别摔倒 "be careful not to fall". The subject is the person who falls; for the thing that tumbles or collapses, use 倒. Also used for throwing someone down in a fight. The result word 倒 reads dǎo here, "fall over".
column6: Xiǎohái zài lùshang shuāidǎo le.
column7: The child fell down on the road.

column3: To bump or crash into something: 撞车 "a car crash", 撞到 + object "bump into", 撞墙 "hit a wall". It also means to meet by chance, as in 撞见 "come across someone". The meaning is more of a hard hit than 碰, which is lighter. 扌 is the hand, 童 the sound.
column6: Tā qí chē zhuàng dào le yī kē shù.
column7: He rode his bike into a tree.

column3: To roll, to turn over and over: 球滚走了 "the ball rolled away", 滚下来 "roll down". Used rudely as a command, 滚！ means "get lost!". It is also "to boil", as in 滚水 "boiling water", the water rolling in the pot. 氵 "water" is the meaning part.
column6: Qiú gǔn dào zhuōzi xiàmian qù le.
column7: The ball rolled under the table.

column3: Slippery, and to slide or slip: 路很滑 "the road is slippery", 滑冰 "ice-skate", 滑雪 "ski", 滑倒 "slip and fall". On a phone, 滑 is to swipe. The sound part 骨 (gǔ) no longer sounds much like huá. 氵 "water" is the meaning part, and fits a wet, slippery surface.
column6: Lù hěn huá, xiǎoxīn diǎnr.
column7: The road is slippery, so be careful.

column3: Read là, it means to leave something behind or forget to bring it: 我的伞落在车上了, 落下 "leave behind", and to fall behind, as in 落后 (also luò there). The usual reading luò is "to fall", as in 落雨 and 落叶. The two readings belong to different meanings, so check which one a sentence needs.
column4: 我把伞落在出租车上了。
column5: 我把傘落在出租車上了。
column6: Wǒ bǎ sǎn là zài chūzūchē shang le.
column7: I left my umbrella in the taxi.

column3: To leak, and to leave out by mistake: 漏水 "water leaks", 屋顶漏雨 "the roof leaks", 漏了一个字 "left out a character", 漏掉 "miss". Also to let information slip, as in 漏消息. 氵 is the water at the left. The picture of 屚 is rain dripping from under a roof.
column6: Wūdǐng lòu yǔ le.
column7: The roof is leaking.

column3: To lose something, and to throw or throw away: 手机丢了 "the phone is lost", 丢钱包 "lose a wallet", 丢人 "lose face, be shameful", 丢掉 "throw away". For a lost item, 丢 is the everyday word, and the object comes before it with 了, or after it with 把: 把钥匙丢了.
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī diū le.
column7: I've lost my phone.

column3: Broken into small pieces, and to break up: 碎了 "it broke", 打碎 "smash", 摔碎 "drop and shatter", 碎片 "fragment". It is used both for something that breaks (a glass) and for something already in small bits (碎纸). 石 "stone" on the left is the meaning part: something hard that cracks. 卒 gives the sound.
column6: Bōlibēi diào zài dìshang, suì le.
column7: The glass fell on the floor and broke.

column3: Rotten, mushy, or in bad shape: 苹果烂了 "the apple went bad", 烂泥 "mud", 破烂 "worn-out junk". In slang it means "bad" or "very poor": 烂电影 "a terrible film", 烂人. Cooked until very soft is also 烂: 炖烂 "stewed until tender". The 火 "fire" on the left fits food cooked till it falls apart.
column6: Zhège píngguǒ làn le.
column7: This apple has gone bad.

column3: To splash or throw liquid: 泼水 "throw water", 把水泼在地上 "splash water on the floor", 泼冷水 "pour cold water on" (to dampen someone's enthusiasm). With 氵 for the water. Another meaning, "bold and spirited", appears in 活泼 "lively", which is also on this list.
column6: Tā bǎ yī pén shuǐ pō zài dìshang.
column7: He splashed a basin of water on the ground.

column3: To spill or sprinkle liquid or small things: 洒水 "sprinkle water", 汤洒了 "the soup spilled", 洒了一地 "spilled all over the floor". It covers accidental spilling as well as sprinkling on purpose. Not to be mixed up with 撒, which spreads loose things like seeds and salt, and is read sǎ too. 氵 is the water.
column6: Tāng sǎ le yī zhuōzi.
column7: The soup spilled all over the table.

column3: To spray or spout out: 喷水 "spray water", 喷泉 "fountain", 喷香水 "spray perfume", 喷漆 "spray paint". Used for anything shot out in a stream, such as water from a pipe. A slang use online is to attack someone with harsh words: 被喷了. 口 "mouth" is the meaning part, as if blowing out.
column6: Shuǐ cóng guǎnzi lǐ pēn chūlái.
column7: Water is spraying out of the pipe.

column3: To give off or send up, such as smoke or steam: 冒烟 "give off smoke", 冒汗 "break out in a sweat", 冒泡 "bubble". Also to brave danger, as in 冒险 "take a risk" and 冒雨 "go out in the rain", and to pass oneself off, as in 冒充. 感冒 "a cold" is a common word that uses it. The top was once a hat 冃 over an eye 目: something covering.
column6: Guō lǐ mào zhe rèqì.
column7: Steam is rising from the pot.

column3: To dye, and also to catch something bad: 染头发 "dye one's hair", 染色 "dye", 染上病 "catch an illness", 染上坏习惯 "pick up a bad habit". 污染 "pollution" has it too. The object is the thing colored, and the color is given with 成 or 上.
column6: Tā bǎ tóufa rǎn chéng le huángsè.
column7: She dyed her hair blond.

column3: Read sǎn, it means loose or scattered: 头发散了 "the hair came loose", 散装 "sold loose", 松散, and powdered medicine. It is a different word from sàn "to disperse", as in 散步 "take a walk" and 散会 "end a meeting", which has the same character with the other tone. The dictionary form here is the loose one.
column6: Shū sǎn le yī dì.
column7: The books were scattered all over the floor.

column3: To steal: 偷东西 "steal things", 偷钱包, and 被偷 "be stolen from". Also "secretly": 偷看 "peek", 偷听 "eavesdrop", 偷笑 "smile to oneself". The thing taken comes after the verb; if it is a thing stolen from you, use 被偷了 or 东西被偷了. 亻 "person" is the meaning part, 俞 the sound.
column6: Yǒu rén tōu le tā de qiánbāo.
column7: Someone stole his wallet.

column3: Thief, the spoken form with the 儿 ending, said "xiǎotōur" and typical of the north. Many speakers say plain 小偷, which means the same. Often with 抓 "catch": 抓小偷儿, or 被小偷偷了. A pickpocket is 扒手. 小 "small" here is for petty thieving.
column6: Xiǎotōur bèi jǐngchá zhuāzhù le.
column7: The thief was caught by the police.

column3: To cheat or deceive: 骗人 "lie to people", 被骗 "be cheated", 受骗上当 "be fooled", 骗钱 "swindle money". The person taken in is the object: 他骗了我. It is a stronger word than 说谎 "tell a lie", since it supposes the other person loses something. 马 on the left is a horse, from the old sense of mounting a horse.
column6: Bié bèi tā piàn le.
column7: Don't be fooled by him.

column3: A swindler, a con man: 他是个骗子 "he is a liar and a cheat", 小心骗子 "beware of fraudsters". 子 is a light, neutral suffix, as in 傻子 and 瞎子. This is a fairly strong word. For scam calls, 诈骗电话 is the common term.
column6: Tā shì ge piànzi, bié xiāngxìn tā.
column7: He is a cheat, so don't trust him.

column3: To snatch or rob, and to compete for something: 抢钱 "rob", 抢包 "snatch a bag", 抢座位 "grab a seat", 抢红包 "grab red envelopes" (on WeChat), 抢票 "scramble for tickets". It can be mild, a race rather than a crime. 抢劫 is the formal word for robbery. 扌 "hand" is the meaning part.
column6: Yǒu rén qiǎng le tā de bāo.
column7: Someone snatched her bag.

column3: To fight with fists, to scuffle: 两个人打架 "two people fight", 跟人打架 "fight with someone". It is a separable verb, so 打了一架 "had a fight". It is physical, unlike 吵架, which is a quarrel with words. There is no object after 打架; name the other person with 跟.
column4: 两个男孩在操场上打架。
column5: 兩個男孩在操場上打架。
column6: Liǎng ge nánhái zài cāochǎng shang dǎjià.
column7: Two boys are fighting on the playground.

column3: To strike a blow, in the sense of attacking or hurting: 打击犯罪 "crack down on crime", 打击对手 "hit the opponent", and a blow, a setback: 受到打击 "suffer a blow", 很大的打击 "a heavy blow". Used for emotional shocks as well. In music, 打击乐 is percussion.
column4: 失败对他是很大的打击。
column5: 失敗對他是很大的打擊。
column6: Shībài duì tā shì hěn dà de dǎjī.
column7: Failure was a heavy blow to him.

column3: To rush in or burst through, often against a rule: 闯红灯 "run a red light", 闯进来 "burst in", 闯祸 "cause trouble", 闯入. It can also be positive, to go out into the world, as in 闯天下 and 走南闯北 "travel widely". The picture is a horse 马 charging through a gate 门.
column6: Tā chuǎng hóngdēng bèi fákuǎn le.
column7: He was fined for running a red light.

column3: To flee, to get away from danger or from a place: 逃命 "run for one's life", 逃学 "skip school", 逃税 "evade taxes", 逃走, 逃跑. It can be used with the person or place escaped from: 从监狱逃了. 辶 "walk" is the meaning part and 兆 gives the sound; the sound part 兆 (zhào) is only a loose match.
column6: Nàge xiǎotōu táo le.
column7: That thief got away.

column3: To run away, to flee on foot: 逃跑的人 "someone who ran away", 被抓住后逃跑 "ran off after being caught". Both characters mean "run away" (逃 flee, 跑 run), so it is an emphatic, concrete word. It is more about running than 逃走, which just means leaving. It rarely takes an object.
column4: 小偷看见警察就逃跑了。
column5: 小偷看見警察就逃跑了。
column6: Xiǎotōu kànjiàn jǐngchá jiù táopǎo le.
column7: The thief ran away when he saw the police.

column3: To escape, to get away: 犯人逃走了 "the prisoner escaped", 趁机逃走 "slip away at the right moment". 走 in Chinese is "to leave", so this just says the person left in order to escape; it does not stress running. Compare 逃跑 on this list, which is more about fleeing at speed.
column4: 他趁大家不注意逃走了。
column5: 他趁大家不注意逃走了。
column6: Tā chèn dàjiā bù zhùyì táozǒu le.
column7: He escaped while nobody was paying attention.

column3: To hide or to dodge: 躲在门后 "hide behind a door", 躲雨 "shelter from the rain", 躲开 "get out of the way", 躲不过 "cannot avoid". The pattern is 躲 + 在 + place for hiding, or 躲 + the thing to avoid. 身 "body" on the left is the meaning part, a body ducking out of the way.
column6: Háizi duǒ zài mén hòumian.
column7: The child is hiding behind the door.

column3: To frighten, or to be frightened: 吓人 "scary", 吓我一跳 "gave me a fright", 吓坏了 "scared out of one's wits", 被吓到. The person frightened is the object: 你吓了我. There is another reading, hè, for threatening, as in 恐吓.
column6: Nǐ xià le wǒ yī tiào!
column7: You gave me a fright!

column3: To bite: 咬一口 "take a bite", 被狗咬了 "was bitten by a dog", 咬牙 "grit one's teeth", 咬住 "bite and hold on". Also for the grip of machine parts and for tight deadlines (咬紧时间). 口 "mouth" is the meaning part and 交 the sound, still close in sound to yǎo, as in 交 jiāo.
column6: Xiǎogǒu yǎo le tā yī kǒu.
column7: The puppy bit him.

column3: Disaster, misfortune. Mostly in compounds: 灾害 "calamity", 灾难 "catastrophe", 天灾 "natural disaster", 救灾 "disaster relief", 火灾 "fire", 水灾 "flood". The shape is a roof 宀 over a fire 火, a house burning.
column6: Zhè shì yī chǎng tiānzāi.
column7: This was a natural disaster.

column3: Calamity, harm brought by nature: 自然灾害 "natural disasters", 减少灾害 "reduce disasters", 气象灾害 "weather-related disasters". A written, general word for floods, droughts, earthquakes and the like, often with 防, 预防 or 造成 ("cause"): 造成灾害. It speaks of the event type, not one particular event; for a single disaster, 灾难 is more usual.
column6: Dìzhèn shì yī zhǒng zìrán zāihài.
column7: An earthquake is a kind of natural disaster.

column3: A disaster that brings suffering, with the human cost in mind: 灾难性的 "catastrophic", 带来灾难 "bring disaster", 经历灾难 "go through a catastrophe". It can be a war, an epidemic or a flood. In everyday speech it is also used for something that went badly wrong: 这简直是一场灾难 "this was a disaster". 难 here is "hardship", read nàn, not nán.
column4: 战争给人们带来了灾难。
column5: 戰爭給人們帶來了災難。
column6: Zhànzhēng gěi rénmen dàilái le zāinàn.
column7: War brought disaster to the people.

column3: A disaster area, the region hit by a flood, quake or storm: 地震灾区 "the quake zone", 去灾区 "go to the affected area", 灾区人民 "people of the stricken region". News and relief reports use it all the time. 区 is "area", the same as in 地区 and 社区.
column6: Yīshēngmen gǎndào le zāiqū.
column7: The doctors rushed to the disaster area.

column3: To give disaster relief, to help the victims of a disaster: 救灾工作 "relief work", 救灾物资 "relief supplies", 抗洪救灾 "fight the flood and give relief". 救 is "save" and 灾 "disaster", with the verb first. It is a separable verb in form but is mostly used as a modifier or in set phrases. 救 has 攵, a hand with a stick, and 求 for sound.
column4: 全国人民都在为救灾出力。
column5: 全國人民都在為救災出力。
column6: Quánguó rénmín dōu zài wèi jiùzāi chūlì.
column7: People across the country are helping with disaster relief.

column3: To be hit by a disaster, to suffer from it: 受灾地区 "the disaster-stricken area", 受灾群众 "affected people", 受灾严重 "badly hit". 受 is "to suffer" and 灾 "disaster", the verb first. It is mostly used in reports and as a modifier. The shape of 受 can be read as a hand passing something to another hand.
column4: 这个县今年受灾很严重。
column5: 這個縣今年受災很嚴重。
column6: Zhège xiàn jīnnián shòuzāi hěn yánzhòng.
column7: This county was badly hit by disaster this year.

column3: A serious fire, in a building or a forest: 发生火灾 "a fire breaks out", 森林火灾 "forest fire", 火灾报警 "fire alarm". It is the written, news word for a big fire. For a small fire, or when speaking, 着火 or 失火 is used. 灾 is itself a roof over a fire 火, so 火灾 repeats the idea.
column4: 昨晚这里发生了一场火灾。
column5: 昨晚這裡發生了一場火災。
column6: Zuówǎn zhèlǐ fāshēng le yī chǎng huǒzāi.
column7: A fire broke out here last night.

column3: A flood, flood damage: 发生水灾 "a flood occurs", 防止水灾 "prevent floods", 水灾严重 "the flooding is severe". It speaks of the harm done by the water, so it is about the disaster, not the water itself. In speech people also say 发大水 for a flood, and 洪水 is the flood water.
column4: 去年夏天这个地区发生了水灾。
column5: 去年夏天這個地區發生了水災。
column6: Qùnián xiàtiān zhège dìqū fāshēng le shuǐzāi.
column7: There was a flood in this area last summer.

column3: An earthquake: 发生地震 "an earthquake occurs", 地震了 "there's an earthquake", 强烈地震, 余震 "aftershock". The size is given in 级: 七级地震 "a magnitude 7 earthquake". 地 is the earth and 震 is "to shake". 震 has the rain 雨 on top and 辰 as the sound.
column6: Zuótiān wǎnshang fāshēng le dìzhèn.
column7: An earthquake happened last night.

column3: A typhoon: 台风来了 "a typhoon is coming", 刮台风 "a typhoon blows", 台风天 "a typhoon day". Typhoon season is in summer and autumn, and weather reports give them numbers or names. The word also means a speaker's stage presence, which is a different word with the same spelling.
column4: 台风要来了，今天别出门。
column5: 颱風要來了，今天別出門。
column6: Táifēng yào lái le, jīntiān bié chūmén.
column7: A typhoon is coming, so don't go out today.

column3: To pollute, and pollution: 污染环境 "pollute the environment", 空气污染 "air pollution", 受到污染 "become polluted", 环境污染. It works as a verb and a noun, and is also used for non-physical contamination, as in 精神污染. 污 is "dirty" with 氵 on the left; 染 "to dye, to taint" is the second part.
column6: Gōngchǎng wūrǎn le héshuǐ.
column7: The factory polluted the river.

column3: Sewage, dirty water: 污水处理 "sewage treatment", 排放污水 "discharge wastewater", 生活污水 "household wastewater". It is a noun, and is used for water from homes and factories. Related: 污染 "pollute". 污 with 氵 "water" is the dirty part. It is a technical word, found in news and reports on the environment.
column6: Zhèxiē wūshuǐ bìxū xiān chǔlǐ.
column7: This sewage has to be treated first.

column3: To rescue something in urgent danger, to give emergency treatment: 抢救病人 "give emergency care to a patient", 抢救文物 "rescue cultural relics", 抢救无效 "treatment failed" (the usual wording when a patient dies). 抢 "to rush, to grab" shows speed and 救 "save" the aim. Used when time is short.
column6: Yīshēng quánlì qiǎngjiù bìngrén.
column7: The doctors did all they could to save the patient.

column3: To call the police, or to raise an alarm: 报警电话 "the emergency number", 马上报警 "call the police at once", 报了警 "reported it". A separable verb. 报 is "to report" and 警 relates to "police" and to warning. In China the number is 110. The top of 警 is 敬 for the sound, and 言 "speech" below.
column4: 他发现小偷后马上报警了。
column5: 他發現小偷後馬上報警了。
column6: Tā fāxiàn xiǎotōu hòu mǎshàng bàojǐng le.
column7: When he found the thief he called the police at once.

column3: Fire fighting, fire protection. Usually before another noun: 消防员 "firefighter", 消防车 "fire engine", 消防队 "fire brigade", 消防安全 "fire safety", 消防通道 "fire exit". It is not used for a fire itself. 消 is "put out" and 防 "to guard against". 消 has 氵 water and 肖 for sound, as in 消失.
column6: Wǒmen xuéxí le xiāofáng zhīshi.
column7: We learned about fire safety.

column3: Unfortunate, and as an adverb "unfortunately": 不幸的事 "an unhappy event", 不幸去世 "died tragically", 他不幸受伤了. Formal, written. It places a misfortune that came by chance, not through fault. Its opposite is 幸运 or 幸福. As a noun it means misfortune: 遭遇不幸.
column6: Tā bùxìng shòu le zhòngshāng.
column7: Unfortunately he was badly injured.

column3: To prevent and treat, mostly a disease or a pollution problem: 防治疾病 "prevent and cure disease", 防治污染 "control pollution", 防治结合 "prevention together with treatment". Written, from public health and the environment. 防 is "guard against" and 治 "to treat, to manage".
column4: 医生在研究怎样防治这种病。
column5: 醫生在研究怎樣防治這種病。
column6: Yīshēng zài yánjiū zěnyàng fángzhì zhè zhǒng bìng.
column7: The doctors are studying how to prevent and treat this illness.

column3: To light, to set on fire: 点燃蜡烛 "light a candle", 点燃火把 "light a torch", 点燃香烟 "light a cigarette". Also figurative, for lighting up hope or passion: 点燃希望. 点 "to light" and 燃 "to burn". 燃 has 火 on the left and 然 for sound; 然 itself once meant "burn" before it became a common ending.
column6: Tā diǎnrán le yī zhī làzhú.
column7: He lit a candle.

column3: Sad, sorrowful, deeply grieved: 悲伤的心情 "a sad mood", 感到悲伤 "feel sad", 悲伤地哭了. It is a strong, serious word, used for loss, not for ordinary unhappiness (难过 is lighter). 悲 has 心 "heart" at the bottom and 非 on top; 伤 means "hurt".
column4: 听到这个消息，她很悲伤。
column5: 聽到這個消息，她很悲傷。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā hěn bēishāng.
column7: She was very sad to hear the news.

column3: A tragedy, in the theatre and in life: 一场悲剧 "a tragedy", 悲剧的结局 "a tragic ending", 避免悲剧. Its pair is 喜剧 "comedy", which is also in this list. 剧 is "drama, play". Often used about real events that were avoidable.
column4: 这是一场可以避免的悲剧。
column5: 這是一場可以避免的悲劇。
column6: Zhè shì yī chǎng kěyǐ bìmiǎn de bēijù.
column7: This is a tragedy that could have been avoided.

column3: To worry, to be troubled: 发愁 "worry", 愁眉苦脸 "a worried look", 不愁吃穿 "never worry about food or clothes", 愁什么 "what's there to worry about". Also the noun "sorrow": 忧愁, 乡愁 "homesickness". Common in speech after 别: 别愁. The heart 心 is the meaning part, with 秋 "autumn" only for the sound.
column6: Bié chóu, bànfǎ zǒng huì yǒu de.
column7: Don't worry, there will always be a way.

column3: To panic, to be flustered: 别慌 "don't panic", 心里发慌 "feel uneasy", 慌了手脚 "lose one's head". After an adjective with 得, it means "unbearably": 累得慌 "dead tired", 闷得慌 "bored to death", 饿得慌. Heart 忄 on the left, 荒 on the right for sound.
column6: Bié huāng, mànmàn shuō.
column7: Don't panic; speak slowly.

column3: In a hurry and flustered, with no time to think: 慌忙站起来 "got up in a rush", 慌忙离开 "left in a flurry", 慌忙说. It is an adverb that goes before the verb and speaks of a past action. Not used with commands. Both characters carry a heart 忄, since the hurry is in the mind.
column6: Tā huāngmáng zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: He stood up in a flurry.

column3: To hesitate, to be unable to decide: 犹豫不决 "be undecided", 犹豫了一下 "hesitated for a moment", 毫不犹豫 "without hesitation", 别犹豫. The two characters work only together. 豫 has 象 "elephant" as its meaning part, but the word has nothing to do with elephants; just learn it as a pair.
column4: 他犹豫了一下，还是说了。
column5: 他猶豫了一下，還是說了。
column6: Tā yóuyù le yīxià, háishi shuō le.
column7: He hesitated for a moment, but said it anyway.

column3: To feel sorry for someone out of love, and to feel pain at losing money or a thing: 心疼孩子 "feel for the child", 看着心疼 "it hurts to watch", 心疼钱 "begrudge the money". The 疼 is "ache". A parent or partner is the usual subject. Literally "heart aches", and used for sympathy rather than for the physical heart.
column4: 看到孩子这么累，妈妈很心疼。
column5: 看到孩子這麼累，媽媽很心疼。
column6: Kàndào háizi zhème lèi, māma hěn xīnténg.
column7: Seeing the child so tired, his mother felt sorry for him.

column3: Pitiful, someone to be pitied: 真可怜 "how pitiful", 可怜的孩子 "the poor child", 可怜巴巴 "looking pitiful". Also "to take pity on": 可怜他. It can sound condescending if said to the person himself. Also "very little", as in 少得可怜 "pitifully few". 怜 has 忄 "heart" and 令 for sound.
column6: Nà zhī xiǎomāo zhēn kělián.
column7: That little cat is so pitiful.

column3: What a pity, it's a shame: 太可惜了 "what a pity", 很可惜 "it's a pity", 可惜的是… "the pity is that…". Used for a missed chance, a waste or a loss, and often to say "unfortunately" at the start of a clause: 可惜他没来. 惜 has 忄 "heart" and 昔 "past", which also gives the sound.
column4: 这么好的机会错过了，真可惜。
column5: 這麼好的機會錯過了，真可惜。
column6: Zhème hǎo de jīhuì cuòguò le, zhēn kěxī.
column7: What a pity to miss such a good chance.

column3: To regret, to feel remorse about something done or not done: 后悔了 "regret it", 后悔莫及 "regret too late", 别后悔 "you'll be sorry". The regretted thing follows, often a clause with 没: 后悔没来. 悔 has 忄 "heart" and 每 for sound.
column4: 我后悔没有早点告诉你。
column5: 我後悔沒有早點告訴你。
column6: Wǒ hòuhuǐ méiyǒu zǎodiǎn gàosu nǐ.
column7: I regret not telling you sooner.

column3: To complain, to grumble about something or somebody: 抱怨工作 "complain about work", 向他抱怨 "complain to him", 抱怨太多. It means voicing a grievance, not a formal complaint (that is 投诉). The thing is the object: 抱怨天气. 抱 is "to hold" and 怨 "resentment": to hold on to a grudge.
column6: Tā zǒngshì bàoyuàn gōngzuò tài duō.
column7: He is always complaining that there is too much work.

column3: To blame, and resentment: 怨他 "blame him", 不能怨别人 "can't blame others", 怨气 "resentment", 埋怨 "complain about". On its own, 怨 is used mostly in the negative: 不怨, 别怨. In daily speech 怪 is the usual verb for "blame". 怨 has 心 "heart" at the bottom.
column6: Zhè shì bù néng yuàn tā.
column7: You can't blame him for this.

column3: To hate, and also to regret strongly: 恨他 "hate him", 恨自己 "hate oneself", 恨不得 "wish one could", 恨铁不成钢. It is much stronger than 讨厌 and used for deep feeling. 恨不得 + verb is a common pattern: 恨不得马上回家. 忄 "heart" is the meaning part and 艮 the sound.
column6: Wǒ hèn tā piàn le wǒ.
column7: I hate him for deceiving me.

column3: To dislike, to find someone or something annoying: 我讨厌… "I can't stand…", 讨厌的人 "an irritating person", 真讨厌 "how annoying". As a verb it takes an object; as an adjective it stands alone. It can also be used playfully, as a mock complaint. 讨 here is "to invite, to bring on" and 厌 "to be sick of".
column6: Wǒ tǎoyàn děng rén.
column7: I hate waiting for people.

column3: Impatient, losing patience: 不耐烦地说 "say impatiently", 很不耐烦 "very impatient", 显得不耐烦 "seem impatient". It goes before a verb with 地 or after 很. The opposite is 耐心. 耐烦 "to have patience" is used almost only in the negative, which is why 不耐烦 is a unit. 烦 has 火 "fire" and 页 for sound: a burning annoyance.
column6: Tā bùnàifán de kàn le kàn biǎo.
column7: He looked at his watch impatiently.

column3: Helpless, with no way out; or "but unfortunately": 无奈地笑了笑 "smiled helplessly", 感到无奈 "feel helpless", 出于无奈 "out of necessity". As a conjunction at the start of a clause it gives the cause that blocks a plan: 本想去，无奈下雨了. 无 is "without" and 奈 "to bear, to cope".
column6: Tā wúnài de xiào le xiào.
column7: He smiled helplessly.

column3: To comfort, to console: 安慰她 "comfort her", 安慰的话 "comforting words", 得到安慰 "find comfort". It is also an adjective, "comforted, relieved": 很安慰. The person comforted is the object, and the words can be added: 安慰了她几句. 慰 has 心 "heart" under 尉, which gives the sound.
column6: Wǒ ānwèi le tā jǐ jù.
column7: I said a few words to comfort her.

column3: To visit or send greetings to people in difficulty: 慰问病人 "visit the sick", 慰问信 "letter of sympathy", 看望慰问, 春节慰问. Formal; the visitor is usually an official, an organization or a group, not an ordinary friend. 慰 is "to comfort" and 问 "to ask after".
column4: 市长去医院慰问了病人。
column5: 市長去醫院慰問了病人。
column6: Shìzhǎng qù yīyuàn wèiwèn le bìngrén.
column7: The mayor visited the patients in the hospital.

column3: To endure, to hold back: 忍着 "hold back", 忍不住 "can't help doing", 忍一忍 "bear it a bit", 容忍 "tolerate", 忍痛. 忍不住 + verb is the common pattern: 忍不住笑了. The shape is a blade 刃 above a heart 心, with 刃 also giving the sound: the pain of a knife pressed to the heart that you hold in.
column6: Wǒ zài yě rěn bù zhù le.
column7: I can't hold it in any longer.

column3: To bear something painful or unpleasant: 忍受痛苦 "endure suffering", 无法忍受 "unbearable", 难以忍受 "hard to bear", 忍受不了 "can't stand it". The object is the pain or the bother, not a person. More formal than 忍 or 受不了, and usual with a strong feeling, such as noise, hunger, or humiliation.
column6: Wǒ wúfǎ rěnshòu zhè zhǒng zàoyīn.
column7: I can't stand this kind of noise.

column3: Proud of one's own or one's group's achievements, in a positive way: 感到自豪 "feel proud", 为…感到自豪 "be proud of…", 令人自豪, 自豪感. It is warmer than 骄傲, which can also mean arrogant. 自 is "self" (an old picture of a nose, which people point to when they mean themselves) and 豪 "grand, bold".
column4: 我为我的国家感到自豪。
column5: 我為我的國家感到自豪。
column6: Wǒ wèi wǒ de guójiā gǎndào zìháo.
column7: I am proud of my country.

column3: To be shocked, astonished, as at bad or very surprising news: 令人震惊 "shocking", 大为震惊, 震惊世界 "shock the world". It can be a verb ("the news shocked us") or an adjective ("we were shocked"). Both characters mean "to shake" and "to be startled", and both fit: 震 has rain 雨 over a sound part, as in 地震, and 惊 has the heart 忄.
column4: 这个消息让大家非常震惊。
column5: 這個消息讓大家非常震驚。
column6: Zhège xiāoxi ràng dàjiā fēicháng zhènjīng.
column7: This news shocked everyone.

column3: An impulse, or to act on one: 一时冲动 "on a sudden impulse", 冲动购物 "impulse buying", 很冲动 "impulsive", 控制冲动 "control the impulse". As an adjective it says someone acts without thinking. 冲 is "to rush" and 动 "to move": a rush that moves you. 别冲动 is common advice before a decision made in anger.
column6: Bié chōngdòng, xiān lěngjìng yīxià.
column7: Don't be rash; calm down first.

column3: Wild, crazy, and also arrogant: 发狂 "go mad", 狂风 "a raging wind", 狂欢 "a wild party", 疯狂, 狂妄 "arrogant". On its own, as in 他太狂了, it means that someone is full of himself. 犭 "dog" is the meaning part, an animal in a frenzy; the right half gives the sound.
column6: Nàge rén tài kuáng le.
column7: That person is too full of himself.

column3: Mad, insane, or wild: 疯了 "gone crazy", 疯子 "madman", 发疯, 疯玩 "play wildly". In speech 你疯了吗？ is a common cry of disbelief, and people say they are 疯了 when overwhelmed, as in 忙疯了. 疯 has 疒 "sickness" and 风 "wind", which gives the sound.
column6: Nǐ fēng le ma?
column7: Have you gone mad?

column3: Crazy, frenzied, wild: 疯狂的行为 "crazy behavior", 疯狂购物 "a shopping spree", 疯狂地爱上 "fall madly in love". As an adjective it comes before 地 and a verb, or before a noun with 的. It can be praise as well as blame: 疯狂的创意 "a wild idea". Both characters repeat the meaning "mad".
column6: Qiúmímen fēngkuáng de hǎnzhe.
column7: The fans were shouting wildly.

column3: To despair, to give up hope; hopeless: 感到绝望 "feel hopeless", 对未来绝望 "despair of the future", 绝望的眼神 "a desperate look". 绝 is "cut off" (with 纟 "thread") and 望 "hope", so the hope is cut off. It is stronger than 失望 "disappointed", and used for deep despair.
column6: Tā duì shēnghuó gǎndào juéwàng.
column7: He felt hopeless about life.

column3: To long for, to yearn: 渴望自由 "long for freedom", 渴望成功, 眼中渴望的神情. It also names the longing: 内心的渴望. It is stronger than 希望, with the feeling of thirst: 渴 is "thirsty" (氵 "water" and 曷), and 望 "to look toward".
column6: Háizimen kěwàng dédào ài.
column7: Children long to be loved.

column3: To expect or hope for something from someone, and the expectation: 对…期望很高 "have high hopes for…", 不负期望 "live up to expectations", 期望他成功. A parent or teacher hopes for a result from another person; it is a little more formal than 希望, and the hope is placed on someone else. 期 here is "to look forward to".
column4: 父母对孩子的期望很高。
column5: 父母對孩子的期望很高。
column6: Fùmǔ duì háizi de qīwàng hěn gāo.
column7: Parents have high hopes for their children.

column3: A wish or a will: 愿意 "be willing", 心愿 "wish", 志愿 "volunteer, ambition", 自愿 "voluntary". On its own it is the formal wish, as in 愿你幸福 "may you be happy" and 祝愿. 愿 is "wish" on top of 心 "heart", which also fits the meaning part.
column6: Yuàn nǐ yīqiè shùnlì!
column7: May everything go well for you!

column3: Voluntary, of one's own free will: 自愿参加 "take part voluntarily", 出于自愿 "of one's own will", 自愿原则. It goes before a verb as an adverb or after 是 as 是…的: 是自愿的. Its opposite is 被迫 "forced". 自 "self" + 愿 "wish": your own wish.
column4: 参加这个活动是自愿的。
column5: 參加這個活動是自願的。
column6: Cānjiā zhège huódòng shì zìyuàn de.
column7: Taking part in this activity is voluntary.

column3: Impressions, thoughts after an experience: 谈感想 "share one's thoughts", 读后感想 "thoughts after reading", 请说说你的感想 "please say what you thought". It names what you feel after something you saw or did, often in a speech or in an essay, and takes 谈, 发表 or 有. 感 "feel" + 想 "think".
column6: Qǐng tántan nǐ de gǎnxiǎng.
column7: Please tell us what you thought of it.

column3: Mindset, attitude of mind: 好心态 "a good attitude", 调整心态 "adjust one's mindset", 心态平和 "a calm frame of mind". It describes a lasting way of thinking about things, more than a mood. Often used for work, exams and hard times, with 保持 or 调整. 心 "heart" + 态 "manner, state".
column6: Bǎochí hǎo xīntài hěn zhòngyào.
column7: It is important to keep a good attitude.

column3: Romantic love, and to be in a relationship: 谈恋爱 "date, be in love", 恋爱结婚 "marry for love", 初恋 "first love". The usual verb is 谈, as in 谈恋爱. 恋爱 is the state, not a single act; one does not "恋爱 someone" directly. 恋 is "attachment" and 爱 "love". The apostrophe in the pinyin keeps the two syllables apart.
column6: Tāmen zhèngzài tán liàn'ài.
column7: They are going out together.

column3: Romantic, in the sense of candlelit dinners and poetic gestures: 很浪漫 "very romantic", 浪漫的爱情, 浪漫的夜晚. It speaks of atmosphere and gestures, not of love itself (that is 恋爱). It can also mean "unrealistic", as in the arts movement, 浪漫主义 "Romanticism".
column4: 这家餐厅的气氛很浪漫。
column5: 這家餐廳的氣氛很浪漫。
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng de qìfēn hěn làngmàn.
column7: The atmosphere in this restaurant is very romantic.

column3: To enjoy, and the enjoyment: 享受生活 "enjoy life", 享受美食, 享受假期, 一种享受 "a pleasure". It can be used with a thing or an experience, for enjoying it fully and slowly. It also means to have a right to something, as in 享受待遇 "receive benefits". 享 was a picture of an ancestral shrine, and 受 is "to receive".
column6: Wǒ hěn xiǎngshòu zhèyàng de shēnghuó.
column7: I really enjoy this kind of life.

column3: To appreciate, to admire: 欣赏音乐 "enjoy music", 欣赏风景 "enjoy the scenery", 欣赏他的才华 "admire his talent". With a thing, it means taking time to look at it with pleasure; with a person, it means to think highly of him. 欣 is "glad" with 欠 and 赏 "to reward" has 贝 "shell, money" at the bottom.
column6: Wǒ hěn xīnshǎng tā de yǒngqì.
column7: I admire his courage.

column3: Energy, vitality: 充满活力 "full of life", 有活力 "lively", 缺乏活力 "lacking energy", 青春活力. It describes people, teams, cities and companies, and is a positive word. 活 is "alive" and 力 "strength", an old picture of a plough or of an arm, which stands for strength.
column6: Niánqīngrén chōngmǎn huólì.
column7: Young people are full of energy.

column3: Friendship: 深厚的友谊 "a deep friendship", 珍惜友谊 "treasure friendship", 友谊长存, 建立友谊. It is a word for the bond between people or between nations, and sounds more formal than 朋友关系. It always names the relationship; for being friends, you say 做朋友. 友 is "friend" and 谊 "good will".
column4: 我们的友谊已经十年了。
column5: 我們的友誼已經十年了。
column6: Wǒmen de yǒuyì yǐjīng shí nián le.
column7: Our friendship has lasted ten years.

column3: Leisure, relaxing in free time: 休闲活动 "leisure activities", 休闲服 "casual clothes", 休闲娱乐, 休闲时间. Often as a modifier of another noun. It stresses relaxed, unhurried time, as opposed to work. In speech, 休息 is "to rest", while 休闲 is the pastime. 休 is a person 亻 resting by a tree 木.
column6: Zhōumò wǒ xǐhuan zài jiā xiūxián.
column7: At weekends I like to relax at home.

column3: Humor, funny: 很幽默 "very funny", 幽默感 "sense of humor", 幽默的人, 幽默地说. A borrowed word from English "humor", chosen for its sound; the characters 幽 "quiet, hidden" and 默 "silent" do not carry the meaning. It names a witty, light kind of fun, not the broad kind (that is 搞笑).
column6: Tā shuōhuà hěn yōumò.
column7: He is very funny when he talks.

column3: Happy, cheerful, carefree: 过得很快活 "have a good time", 快快活活 "merrily", 快活的日子. It is warmer and more informal than 快乐 and is mostly used for a person's life or mood, not for a festival. 活 is read huo, neutral, here. 快 "quick, glad" + 活 "lively".
column6: Tāmen guò de hěn kuàihuo.
column7: They lead a happy life.

column3: Lively, vivacious: 活泼可爱 "lively and lovable", 性格活泼 "outgoing character", 活泼的孩子. Said of children and young people, and also of styles and designs. In chemistry it means "reactive". 泼 is read po, neutral, in this word, but pō in 泼水.
column6: Zhège háizi hěn huópo.
column7: This child is very lively.

column3: Idle, free of work: 很闲 "have time on one's hands", 闲着 "sit idle", 有空闲 "have spare time", 闲聊 "chat idly", 闲话. It also has a slight negative sense of "doing nothing", as in 闲人 "idler". Its shape is a wooden bar 木 in a doorway 门; an older meaning is an enclosure or barrier.
column6: Tā jīntiān hěn xián.
column7: He has nothing to do today.

column3: To rest, to take a break: 歇一会儿 "rest a while", 歇歇 "have a rest", 歇脚 "stop for a rest", 歇业 "close a shop". It is a spoken word, used mostly for a short break in the middle of work or a walk. 歇 has 欠 (a yawning mouth) on the right, which fits tiredness, and 曷 for the sound.
column6: Lèi le jiù xiē yīhuìr ba.
column7: If you're tired, rest a while.

column3: Clever, intelligent: 聪明的孩子 "a bright child", 很聪明 "very clever", 小聪明 "petty cleverness". It speaks of quick wit and learning. Said of people and animals; used about an idea or a choice, it means "wise". 聪 has 耳 "ear" and 明 "bright", from the idea of sharp hearing and sight. 明 is neutral here.
column6: Zhège háizi hěn cōngming.
column7: This child is very clever.

column3: Foolish, silly: 傻瓜 "fool", 傻笑 "smile foolishly", 装傻 "play dumb", 发傻 "stare blankly". Between friends it is playful: 傻孩子, 你真傻. It can be harsher about someone's judgement. 亻 "person" is the meaning part. Plain 笨 means "slow to learn", while 傻 is about silly behavior.
column6: Wǒ zhēn shǎ, zěnme méi xiǎngdào ne?
column7: How silly of me not to have thought of it!

column3: Bold, daring: 大胆地说 "say boldly", 大胆尝试 "dare to try", 胆子大 "have courage", 大胆的想法 "a daring idea". Can also be rude: 大胆！ "how dare you!". Positive in encouragement, as in 大胆去做. 大 "big" + 胆 "gallbladder", which in Chinese is the seat of courage. 胆 has ⺼ "flesh" and 旦 for the sound.
column4: 她大胆地说出了自己的想法。
column5: 她大膽地說出了自己的想法。
column6: Tā dàdǎn de shuōchū le zìjǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
column7: She boldly spoke her mind.

column3: Timid, easily scared: 胆小的人 "a timid person", 胆小鬼 "coward", 胆子小 "have little courage". Said of a child, an animal or an adult. 胆小如鼠 "timid as a mouse" is a set phrase. The opposite is 大胆. 胆 "gallbladder", the seat of courage, + 小 "small".
column6: Tā dǎnxiǎo, bù gǎn yī ge rén shuì.
column7: He is timid and dares not sleep alone.

column3: Polite, formal; to stand on ceremony: 别客气 "you're welcome, make yourself at home", 不用客气, 太客气了 "you're too kind", 客客气气 "very politely". It is a courtesy word used when offering and when answering thanks. With people close to you, being 客气 means you keep your distance. 客 is a "guest" under a roof; 气 is neutral here.
column6: Bùyòng kèqi, qǐng zuò.
column7: No need to stand on ceremony; please sit.

column3: Courtesy, manners; polite: 有礼貌 "polite", 没礼貌 "rude", 讲礼貌 "be polite", 礼貌用语 "polite expressions". It can be a noun ("manners") and an adjective ("polite"). Used for children and strangers, with 对…有礼貌: 对老人有礼貌. 礼 is "ritual, courtesy" and 貌 "appearance", so the outward side of good behavior.
column6: Duì lǎorén yào yǒu lǐmào.
column7: You must be polite to old people.

column3: Hard-working, diligent: 勤奋学习 "study hard", 勤奋的学生, 很勤奋. Positive, for study and work. It means steady effort over time, not just a burst. 勤 has 力 "strength" and 奋 has 大 over 田 "field": a man striving in the fields. The traditional 奮 also had a bird 隹 in it.
column6: Tā xuéxí hěn qínfèn.
column7: He studies diligently.

column3: Humble and open to advice: 虚心学习 "learn humbly", 虚心听取意见 "listen humbly to opinions", 虚心的态度. It is praise: someone who knows they can still learn. Its opposite is 骄傲 or 自满. 虚 is "empty" and 心 "heart", so the heart is empty of pride, with room for more.
column6: Tā xūxīn de tīngqǔ yìjiàn.
column7: He listens humbly to advice.

column3: Sincere, genuine: 真诚的态度 "a sincere attitude", 真诚地道歉 "apologize sincerely", 待人真诚 "treat people sincerely". It is stronger than 诚实 "honest": it is the warmth and openness of someone who means what they say. 诚 has 讠 "speech" and 成, which gives the sound.
column6: Tā de dàoqiàn hěn zhēnchéng.
column7: His apology was sincere.

column3: Mild, gentle: 性格温和 "a gentle nature", 温和的语气 "a gentle tone", 气候温和 "a mild climate". It can be said of a person, a way of speaking, the weather or a medicine. It has no "weak" sense. 温 has 氵 "water" and 昷 for the sound; 和 is read hé here.
column6: Tā shuōhuà de shēngyīn hěn wēnhé.
column7: He has a gentle voice.

column3: Terrific, formidable, in a good or a bad sense: 你真厉害 "you're amazing", 厉害的老师 "a tough teacher", 疼得厉害 "it hurts terribly", 热得厉害. As praise, it is the everyday way to say "impressive". After 得 it means "very": 冷得厉害. 害 is neutral in 厉害.
column6: Tā de Yīngyǔ shuō de zhēn lìhai.
column7: His English is really impressive.

column3: Stern, strict, harsh: 严厉的老师 "a strict teacher", 严厉批评 "criticize sharply", 严厉打击 "crack down hard". Said of a person's manner or a punishment. It is stronger than 严格, which is just "strict about rules". 严 and 厉 both mean strict.
column6: Lǎoshī duì xuésheng hěn yánlì.
column7: The teacher is very strict with his students.

column3: Serious, solemn, stern: 表情严肃 "a serious look", 严肃的话题 "a serious topic", 严肃处理 "deal with it strictly", 严肃地说. It speaks of a grave atmosphere or manner, and also of a rule being applied seriously. Unlike 认真, which is about taking care in doing something, 严肃 is about gravity.
column6: Tā de biǎoqíng hěn yánsù.
column7: His expression is very serious.

column3: Firm, resolute: 态度坚定 "a firm attitude", 坚定的信念 "unshakable belief", 坚定地说, 坚定不移. It is about the will, not a thing's hardness. As a verb it means "to strengthen one's resolve": 坚定决心. 坚 is hard and 定 "set": hard-set. 坚 has 土 "earth" at the bottom.
column6: Tā de tàidù hěn jiāndìng.
column7: Her attitude is very firm.

column3: Hard, arduous, with real hardship: 艰苦的环境 "a harsh environment", 生活艰苦, 艰苦奋斗 "work hard in difficult conditions". It is used for living conditions, work and times that are hard, as in a poor or remote place. A written, serious word. 艰 and 苦 both mean "hard"; 苦 is the bitter taste, with 艹 on top.
column6: Shānqū de shēnghuó hěn jiānkǔ.
column7: Life in the mountains is hard.

column3: Temper, disposition: 脾气好 "good-natured", 脾气不好 "bad-tempered", 发脾气 "lose one's temper", 好脾气. It can mean a character in general or a bad temper, so 他有脾气 can mean "he has a temper". 脾 is the spleen, an organ, so it has ⺼ "flesh". 气 is neutral.
column6: Tā píqi bù hǎo, róngyì shēngqì.
column7: He has a bad temper and gets angry easily.

column3: Face, social prestige: 爱面子 "care about appearances", 给面子 "show respect", 丢面子 "lose face", 没面子, 不给面子. In Chinese social life it is about how others see you. The other meaning, the outer surface of something, is rare. 面 is the picture of a face, and 子 is a neutral suffix.
column6: Tā hěn ài miànzi.
column7: He cares a lot about saving face.

column3: Hard, tiring; to take trouble: 你辛苦了 "thank you for your hard work", 很辛苦 "very hard going", 辛辛苦苦 "toiling". Said to thank someone for work done, 您辛苦了 is a polite phrase. As a command, 辛苦你了 asks a favor. 辛 once pictured a tool for branding, and now stands for "bitter, hard". 苦 is "bitter", with 艹.
column4: 你辛苦了，快坐下休息吧。
column5: 你辛苦了，快坐下休息吧。
column6: Nǐ xīnkǔ le, kuài zuòxià xiūxi ba.
column7: You've worked hard; sit down and rest.

column3: Patience, patient: 有耐心 "be patient", 耐心地等 "wait patiently", 耐心地解释, 缺乏耐心. As a noun it goes with 有 and 没有. As an adjective it goes before the verb: 耐心地. It is the opposite of 不耐烦. 耐 is "to endure" and 心 "heart".
column6: Lǎoshī hěn yǒu nàixīn.
column7: The teacher is very patient.

column3: Sensitive, easily affected: 对声音敏感 "sensitive to sound", 敏感话题 "a sensitive topic", 皮肤敏感 "sensitive skin", 太敏感. It may be a quality of the senses, or the mind. It can be a fault in a person who takes things too personally, but a good thing in a scientist or an investor, who notices details. 敏 is "quick" and 感 "feel".
column6: Tā duì shēngyīn hěn mǐngǎn.
column7: She is very sensitive to sound.

column3: Bad, harmful, unhealthy: 不良习惯 "a bad habit", 不良影响 "harmful influence", 营养不良 "malnutrition", 不良少年. It is a written, formal word that comes before a noun, in a mild, official tone for habits, influence, or effects. It is not used as a plain adjective after 很. 不 "not" + 良 "good".
column6: Áoyè shì yī zhǒng bùliáng xíguàn.
column7: Staying up late is a bad habit.

column3: Cultivation, self-development in character and manners: 有修养 "well-bred, cultivated", 个人修养, 文化修养, 艺术修养. It describes a person's inner quality that shows in behavior: a person 有修养 is calm and polite. 修 is "to repair, to cultivate" and 养 "to nourish". It can also be skill in a field: 艺术修养.
column4: 他是一个很有修养的人。
column5: 他是一個很有修養的人。
column6: Tā shì yī ge hěn yǒu xiūyǎng de rén.
column7: He is a very cultivated person.

column3: Strenuous, hard to do; to find it a strain: 很吃力 "very hard going", 做得吃力 "do it with difficulty", 吃力不讨好 "a thankless task". After 得 or 感到, it says that something costs real effort. 吃 is "to eat", used as "to take on", and 力 "strength": it takes strength.
column4: 这个工作他做得有点吃力。
column5: 這個工作他做得有點吃力。
column6: Zhège gōngzuò tā zuò de yǒudiǎn chīlì.
column7: He finds this job a bit of a strain.

column3: To pay a formal visit to someone: 拜访老师 "call on a teacher", 拜访客户 "visit a client", 登门拜访 "visit someone at home". Polite and written, it shows respect for the person visited and is used for professional or social calls, not for dropping in on friends (that is 去看). 拜 is a pair of hands put together in respect, and 访 "to visit, to ask" has 讠 "speech".
column4: 我明天去拜访一位老师。
column5: 我明天去拜訪一位老師。
column6: Wǒ míngtiān qù bàifǎng yī wèi lǎoshī.
column7: Tomorrow I am going to call on a teacher.

column3: To invite, and an invitation: 邀请朋友来家里 "invite a friend over", 邀请你参加 + event, 接受邀请 "accept an invitation", 邀请函 "an invitation letter". The pattern is 邀请 + person + 参加/去 + event. It is more formal than 请, which can also mean "invite" in speech, and it is used for events more than for a meal. 邀 has 辶 "walk" and 请 "to request".
column4: 他邀请我参加他的婚礼。
column5: 他邀請我參加他的婚禮。
column6: Tā yāoqǐng wǒ cānjiā tā de hūnlǐ.
column7: He invited me to his wedding.

column3: To accompany, to keep someone company: 陪我去 "go with me", 陪孩子玩 "play with the child", 陪客人 "keep a guest company", 陪伴. The accompanied person comes right after 陪, and then what you do together: 陪妈妈去医院. It is a favor or a duty to be there for someone. 阝 on the left is the "hill" sign, and 咅 gives the sound.
column6: Wǒ péi māma qù yīyuàn.
column7: I am going to the hospital with my mother.

column3: A gift, and courtesy or ceremony: 送礼 "give a gift", 礼物 "present", 礼貌 "politeness", 礼节 "etiquette", 婚礼 "wedding", 行礼 "bow, salute". On its own it is mainly a gift in 送礼 and 收礼. The left 礻 is the sign for spirits and rites, found in 祝 and 神.
column6: Guònián yào gěi zhǎngbèi sòng lǐ.
column7: At New Year you should give gifts to the older generation.

column3: To give as a present, formal and written: 赠书 "give a book", 赠言 "parting words", 赠予 "bestow", 赠品 "freebie". Given by a person to another in a polite or official way, and often the gift of an organization. In daily speech 送 is used instead. 贝 "shell, money" is the meaning part, as in many words about wealth or giving, and 曾 gives the sound.
column6: Tā zèng le wǒ yī běn shū.
column7: She gave me a book as a present.

column3: To give as a gift, often free: 赠送礼品 "give a gift", 免费赠送 "give away for free", 买一赠送一 "buy one, get one". Common in shops and promotions, and for presents between organizations. Between friends people say 送. 赠 is the formal "present" and 送 is "send, give".
column6: Shāngdiàn zèngsòng yī ge xiǎo lǐwù.
column7: The shop gives a small gift.

column3: To offer or present with respect, to donate: 献花 "present flowers", 献血 "donate blood", 献给 + person "dedicate to", 贡献 "contribute", 奉献 "devote". Often something offered to a person you respect, a cause or a country. 献 is mostly in compounds; on its own, you see 献花 and 献血 most.
column6: Xuéshengmen xiàng lǎoshī xiàn huā.
column7: The students presented flowers to the teacher.

column3: To congratulate, and congratulations: 祝贺你 "congratulations to you", 向他祝贺 "congratulate him", 表示祝贺 "offer congratulations", 祝贺成功. It is for a person's success or a happy event, and takes the person as object. 祝 shows a person kneeling before an altar, and 贺 puts 加 "add" over 贝 "wealth": adding to someone's fortune.
column6: Zhùhè nǐ kǎoshàng le dàxué!
column7: Congratulations on getting into university!

column3: To respect and honor a person, and respectful: 尊敬老师 "respect teachers", 受人尊敬 "be respected", 令人尊敬 "worthy of respect". It is for a person you look up to because of age, character or position. In letters, 尊敬的 + title opens a formal address, like "Dear". 尊 has a hand 寸 offering a vessel of wine 酋.
column6: Wǒmen dōu hěn zūnjìng tā.
column7: We all respect him.

column3: To respect, to treat with consideration; respect: 尊重别人 "respect others", 尊重选择 "respect a choice", 互相尊重 "mutual respect", 受到尊重. Unlike 尊敬, which looks up to a person, 尊重 can apply to opinions, rules and rights as well as to people. It means not overriding or looking down on something. 重 is read zhòng here.
column4: 我们要尊重别人的选择。
column5: 我們要尊重別人的選擇。
column6: Wǒmen yào zūnzhòng biéren de xuǎnzé.
column7: We must respect other people's choices.

column3: Concern, care for people, shown with warmth: 关怀老人 "show care for the elderly", 得到关怀, 亲切的关怀, 人文关怀 "humane concern". Written and used for institutions or leaders caring for others, and for an attentive person. 关 is "to be concerned" and 怀 is "to cherish" (the heart 忄).
column6: Lǎoshī hěn guānhuái měi ge xuésheng.
column7: The teacher cares about every student.

column3: A return for effort or kindness; to repay: 得到回报 "be rewarded", 回报社会 "give back to society", 投资回报 "return on investment", 没有回报. As a noun, it is the result of work or money put in. As a verb, it means to repay a kindness. 回 "return" + 报 "report, repay". It can also mean to report back, in a work context.
column6: Tā de nǔlì dédào le huíbào.
column7: His efforts were rewarded.

column3: To repay a kindness or favor: 报答父母 "repay one's parents", 报答恩情 "repay a debt of gratitude", 无以报答 "I can't repay you enough". It is used only for good turns and is somewhat formal and emotional. 回报 is more about results; 报答 is about gratitude. 答 here is "to answer, to respond" in the sense of answering a kindness.
column4: 我一定会报答你的恩情。
column5: 我一定會報答你的恩情。
column6: Wǒ yīdìng huì bàodá nǐ de ēnqíng.
column7: I will repay your kindness for sure.

column3: Greeting card: 新年贺卡 "New Year card", 生日贺卡 "birthday card", 寄贺卡 "send a card", 电子贺卡 "e-card". 贺 is "to congratulate" and 卡 is a loan from English "card". 卡 is read kǎ in this sense, and it is drawn as 上 over 下, like something squeezed between up and down; it also has the reading qiǎ, "to be stuck".
column4: 我给朋友寄了一张贺卡。
column5: 我給朋友寄了一張賀卡。
column6: Wǒ gěi péngyou jì le yī zhāng hèkǎ.
column7: I sent my friend a greeting card.

column3: To share something good, such as joy, experience or information: 分享快乐 "share joy", 分享经验 "share experience", 分享照片 "share photos", 和大家分享. On social media, 分享 is the "share" button. It is for giving others a part of something you enjoy, not for dividing a cost (that is 分担). 享 "to enjoy".
column4: 我想和大家分享这个好消息。
column5: 我想和大家分享這個好消息。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng hé dàjiā fēnxiǎng zhège hǎo xiāoxi.
column7: I'd like to share this good news with everyone.

column3: Too, excessively, usually of something undesirable: 过于紧张 "too nervous", 过于简单 "too simple", 过于担心 "worry too much", 不要过于… "don't be too…". It is a written word that goes before an adjective or verb. More formal than 太, and not used for praise: you cannot say 过于好. 过 here is "beyond", the same as in 过度.
column4: 他过于紧张，说不出话来。
column5: 他過於緊張，說不出話來。
column6: Tā guòyú jǐnzhāng, shuō bu chū huà lái.
column7: He was too nervous to say a word.

column3: Excessive, too much, to excess: 过度劳累 "overwork", 过度使用 "overuse", 过度饮酒 "drink to excess", 消费过度. It goes before a verb or noun as a modifier and is neutral to negative; the thing is too much of what is usually fine. 过 "beyond" + 度 "degree, measure": past the limit.
column4: 过度使用手机对眼睛不好。
column5: 過度使用手機對眼睛不好。
column6: Guòdù shǐyòng shǒujī duì yǎnjing bù hǎo.
column7: Overusing a phone is bad for the eyes.
